rules.title: SLA breach rate above threshold
rules.whatItMeans: The SLA breach rate exceeds threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: The headline SLA measure. Only meaningful alongside the configuration findings, because a breach rate computed on misconfigured SLAs measures the configuration rather than the service.
rules.sourceTables: task_sla breach records, SLA definitions, incident volume
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(breached SLAs) / COUNT(SLAs attached), by definition and by group
rules.threshold: Threshold from the customer's own commitment; default 10%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio, conditional on SLA configuration being sound. Report ITSM-003 and ITSM-012 alongside.
rules.evidenceToShow: Breach rate by definition, group and priority, with breach timing distribution and the SLA configuration for each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Breaches caused by SLA misconfiguration rather than service failure. Report the configuration findings first.
rules.crossDomainLink: Only valid once the SLA configuration findings are resolved

rules.title: SLA paused or cancelled at abnormal rates (gaming)
rules.whatItMeans: SLA records are being paused or cancelled at abnormal rates.
rules.whyItMatters: Pause and cancel stop the clock. Abnormal rates suggest the mechanism is being used to manage the metric rather than to reflect genuine waiting. A control integrity finding rather than a performance one.
rules.sourceTables: task_sla pause and cancel events, duration in paused state
rules.detectionLogic: Pause and cancel rates by group and by definition, against the estate distribution; plus paused duration exceeding active duration
rules.threshold: Default flag at 2x the estate mean rate
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the rates. The gaming interpretation is inferred and should be stated as such.
rules.evidenceToShow: Pause and cancel rates by group, paused versus active duration, the pause reasons where captured, and the on-hold state correlation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate high-pause workload, such as incidents awaiting third-party vendors.
rules.crossDomainLink: Control integrity; route to audit as well as operations

rules.title: Resolution time distribution with a spike immediately before SLA expiry
rules.whatItMeans: The resolution time distribution shows a spike immediately before SLA expiry.
rules.whyItMatters: Work is being timed to the target rather than to the problem. Statistically unmistakable and difficult to explain any other way.
rules.sourceTables: incident resolution timestamps, task_sla target times, resolution-to-target interval distribution
rules.detectionLogic: Resolution time distribution relative to SLA target; flag a spike in the final decile before expiry
rules.threshold: Spike threshold default 2x the expected density for that interval
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the distribution. The interpretation is strongly evidenced by the shape.
rules.evidenceToShow: Resolution timing histogram relative to target, by group and priority, with the expected distribution overlaid.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuine prioritisation pressure producing a natural clustering near targets.
rules.crossDomainLink: Control integrity; strong evidence of metric management

rules.title: Incidents resolved and closed within seconds of creation (bulk closure)
rules.whatItMeans: Incidents are resolved and closed within seconds of creation, in volume.
rules.whyItMatters: Bulk closure. Either an automated process is closing records without action, or someone is clearing a backlog by closing it.
rules.sourceTables: incident creation, resolution and closure timestamps, closing user
rules.detectionLogic: Incidents whose create-to-close interval is below threshold, grouped by closing user and by time window
rules.threshold: Default threshold 60 seconds
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the interval arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by closing user and time window, the close codes used, resolution note state, and whether they clustered in bursts.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate automated resolution for self-healing conditions.
rules.crossDomainLink: Control integrity; distorts every volume and resolution metric

rules.title: Backlog ageing beyond threshold by priority
rules.whatItMeans: The incident backlog is ageing beyond threshold, by priority band.
rules.whyItMatters: Backlog age by priority is what tells you whether the queue is being worked or merely held. A growing P2 backlog with a healthy P1 backlog is a capacity signal.
rules.sourceTables: Open incident ages by priority
rules.detectionLogic: Open incidents exceeding age threshold per priority band, with trend
rules.threshold: Age thresholds per priority; defaults 2 days P1, 5 days P2, 15 days P3
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on age arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Age distribution by priority and group, backlog trend, and the oldest records with their last activity date.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Records legitimately parked awaiting a third party, correctly on hold.

rules.title: P1 raised manually where automated conditions existed
rules.whatItMeans: P1 incidents are being raised manually in situations where automated conditions existed and should have triggered.
rules.whyItMatters: The automation was configured and did not fire, so the detection depended on a human noticing. Detection time is the difference between a four-minute response and a seventeen-minute one.
rules.sourceTables: P1 incidents, their creation source, alert and event correlation in the preceding window
rules.detectionLogic: Manually created P1 incidents with a correlated alert in the preceding window that did not auto-create
rules.threshold: Correlation window configurable, default 30 minutes
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — correlation between alert and incident is circumstantial without an explicit link.
rules.evidenceToShow: The incident, the correlated alert, the alert rule state, and the time between alert and manual creation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely human-detected issues with a coincidental alert.

rules.title: P1 volume without corresponding Problem records
rules.whatItMeans: P1 volume exists with no corresponding Problem records.
rules.whyItMatters: Major incidents are being resolved and never analysed. The same cause will produce the same P1 again, and each occurrence starts from nothing.
rules.sourceTables: P1 incident volume, linked Problem records
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(P1 incidents with no linked Problem) / COUNT(P1 incidents)
rules.threshold: Default threshold 30%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the link check.
rules.evidenceToShow: P1 list with Problem linkage state, their close codes, and the recurrence pattern among unanalysed P1s.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: P1s with a genuinely one-off external cause.

rules.title: Incidents created by the same caller repeatedly for the same issue (unresolved root cause)
rules.whatItMeans: The same caller raises repeated incidents for the same issue.
rules.whyItMatters: The underlying cause is not being resolved. Each incident is closed individually and the pattern is invisible because nothing aggregates across callers.
rules.sourceTables: incident caller, short description similarity, creation timing
rules.detectionLogic: Caller and description-cluster pairs with repeat volume above threshold in the window
rules.threshold: Similarity threshold and repeat count configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — clustering by description similarity.
rules.evidenceToShow: Caller, the incident cluster, resolution codes used across them, and whether a Problem exists.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Caller in a role that legitimately generates similar requests.

rules.title: First-call resolution rate declining
rules.whatItMeans: The first-call resolution rate is declining over time.
rules.whyItMatters: A capability or knowledge trend. Declining FCR with stable volume usually means knowledge is not keeping pace with the estate.
rules.sourceTables: incident resolution at first assignment, reassignment count, trend across windows
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(incidents resolved with zero reassignments) / COUNT(resolved), trended
rules.threshold: Requires at least 3 windows
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio. Trend confidence from window count.
rules.evidenceToShow: FCR trend overall and by group, with volume and category mix for context.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Category mix shifted toward genuinely harder work.

rules.title: Assignment to an individual rather than a group
rules.whatItMeans: Incidents are assigned to an individual rather than to a group.
rules.whyItMatters: The ticket is invisible to the team and stalls when that person is unavailable. Creates key-person dependency in the queue.
rules.sourceTables: incident.assigned_to population without assignment_group, or assignment directly to individuals
rules.detectionLogic: Incidents with assigned_to populated and assignment_group empty, or assignment patterns concentrated on individuals
rules.threshold: Report as a ratio and by individual
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio, distribution by individual, and the resolution time for individually assigned versus group assigned incidents.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Specialist work where individual assignment is the operating model.

rules.title: On-hold reason not captured
rules.whatItMeans: The on-hold reason is not captured when incidents are placed on hold.
rules.whyItMatters: On-hold time is excluded from SLA and nobody knows why. Cannot distinguish legitimate vendor waits from parking, which makes ITSM-034 impossible to interpret.
rules.sourceTables: incident on-hold state transitions, hold reason field population
rules.detectionLogic: On-hold transitions with empty hold reason
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio by group, the hold duration distribution, and the SLA pause time attributable to unreasoned holds.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Hold reason captured in work notes instead.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 — make the field mandatory on transition

rules.title: Incidents resolved by the caller themselves
rules.whatItMeans: Incidents are being resolved by the caller themselves.
rules.whyItMatters: Either the caller has fulfiller access they should not have, or resolution is being recorded under the wrong identity. The first is an access finding.
rules.sourceTables: incident caller_id and resolved_by comparison, caller role check
rules.detectionLogic: Resolved incidents where caller_id equals resolved_by, joined to the caller's role set
rules.threshold: Report separately for callers with and without fulfiller roles
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by caller, their role set, the close codes used, and whether they hold fulfiller access.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate self-service resolution model.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3; escalate to access review where the caller should not have fulfiller roles

rules.title: No major incident process configured despite P1 volume
rules.whatItMeans: No major incident process is configured despite significant P1 volume.
rules.whyItMatters: Major incidents are being handled as ordinary P1s with no communication plan, no war room, no post-incident review and no structured escalation. The process that exists for the worst days does not exist.
rules.sourceTables: Major incident configuration, P1 volume, major incident record count
rules.detectionLogic: P1 volume above threshold with zero or near-zero major incident records and no major incident configuration
rules.threshold: P1 volume threshold configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration and record absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: P1 volume, major incident record count, the configuration state, and the P1s that met major incident criteria by duration or impact.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Major incident process run outside ServiceNow with documented evidence.
rules.crossDomainLink: Structural absence of the process that matters most

rules.title: Major incident raised with no communication plan or task
rules.whatItMeans: A major incident is raised with no communication plan or communication task.
rules.whyItMatters: During a major incident, stakeholder communication is the thing that fails first and is remembered longest. No plan means it depends on whoever thinks of it.
rules.sourceTables: Major incident records, communication plan and task linkage
rules.detectionLogic: Major incidents with no communication plan record or communication task
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage check.
rules.evidenceToShow: Major incident, duration, affected services, and the absence of communication records.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Communication handled through an external mechanism with evidence.

rules.title: Major incident closed with no post-incident review
rules.whatItMeans: A major incident is closed with no post-incident review.
rules.whyItMatters: The most expensive learning opportunity the organisation gets, discarded. Guarantees the next occurrence starts from the same place.
rules.sourceTables: Major incident closure, PIR record linkage
rules.detectionLogic: Closed major incidents with no linked post-incident review
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage.
rules.evidenceToShow: Major incident list, duration, business impact, and PIR linkage state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: PIR conducted outside ServiceNow with evidence.

rules.title: Major incident with no linked Problem record
rules.whatItMeans: A major incident has no linked Problem record.
rules.whyItMatters: The specific version of ITSM-039 for the incidents that matter most. A major incident with no Problem is a decision not to find out why it happened.
rules.sourceTables: Major incident records, Problem linkage
rules.detectionLogic: Major incidents with no linked Problem
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage.
rules.evidenceToShow: Major incident list with duration, affected services, close code, and Problem linkage state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Cause fully established during the incident and documented in the record.

rules.title: Major incident with no affected service populated
rules.whatItMeans: A major incident has no affected service populated.
rules.whyItMatters: The business impact of a major incident is unrecorded. Reporting to executives is anecdotal, and the incident cannot be aggregated into service reliability figures.
rules.sourceTables: Major incident business_service and affected service fields
rules.detectionLogic: Major incidents with no service reference populated
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Major incident list, the CIs referenced, and whether those CIs have a traversable path to a service.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Infrastructure-level incident with no single service impact.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 1 where the CI path resolves the service, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.crossDomainLink: Joins CMDB-057; often blocked by reachability

rules.title: Major incident timeline gaps (no updates for extended periods)
rules.whatItMeans: Major incident timelines contain gaps with no updates for extended periods.
rules.whyItMatters: The record does not reflect what happened. Post-incident review and any regulatory reporting work from an incomplete timeline.
rules.sourceTables: Major incident journal entries, update timestamps, gap analysis
rules.detectionLogic: Major incidents with update gaps exceeding threshold during the active period
rules.threshold: Gap threshold default 30 minutes during an active major incident
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on timestamp gaps.
rules.evidenceToShow: Major incident, its update timeline with gaps highlighted, duration, and the gap total as a share of incident duration.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Updates captured in an external war-room channel.
rules.crossDomainLink: Post-incident review and regulatory evidence gap

rules.title: Major incident candidate criteria never triggering
rules.whatItMeans: Major incident candidate criteria are configured but never trigger.
rules.whyItMatters: The automatic promotion path does not work, so major incidents depend on a human deciding. Delays declaration, which is the most time-sensitive decision in the process.
rules.sourceTables: Major incident candidate rule configuration, trigger events, manual promotion records
rules.detectionLogic: Candidate criteria configured with zero trigger events, where P1s meeting those criteria exist
rules.threshold: Any occurrence with qualifying P1s present
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on trigger events and criteria evaluation.
rules.evidenceToShow: Criteria configuration, the P1s that met them, the trigger event absence, and the manual promotion timing for those incidents.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Criteria deliberately advisory.

rules.title: Post-incident review actions created but never closed
rules.whatItMeans: Post-incident review actions are created and never closed.
rules.whyItMatters: The review happened, the actions were identified, and nothing was done. Worse than no review, because it creates a documented record of known risks left unaddressed.
rules.sourceTables: PIR action records, state and age
rules.detectionLogic: Open PIR actions beyond age threshold
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 90 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on age arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Action list with age, owner, source major incident, and whether that incident type has recurred since.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Actions deliberately deferred with documented acceptance.

rules.title: Problem process effectively unused — Problem-to-Incident ratio near zero
rules.whatItMeans: The Problem process is effectively unused — the ratio of Problem records to incident volume is near zero.
rules.whyItMatters: Every incident is treated as a first occurrence. Recurring causes are resolved repeatedly at full cost and never removed. This is usually the single largest avoidable cost in an ITSM estate, and almost nobody measures it.
rules.sourceTables: problem record count, incident volume, ratio across the window
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(Problem records created) / COUNT(incidents created) in the window
rules.threshold: Default threshold 0.5%. Escalate below 0.1%.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: The ratio with trend, Problem creation by group, and the incident clusters that should have produced Problems.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Problem management run outside ServiceNow with documented evidence.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — process adoption, not a data fix
rules.crossDomainLink: Root cause of repeated incident cost

rules.title: Recurring incident patterns with no corresponding Problem record
rules.whatItMeans: Recurring incident patterns exist with no corresponding Problem record.
rules.whyItMatters: Names the specific clusters rather than complaining about the ratio. Converts an abstract process criticism into a list of things to act on.
rules.sourceTables: incident short description and category clustering, Problem linkage
rules.detectionLogic: Incident clusters above volume threshold with no linked Problem
rules.threshold: Cluster volume threshold and similarity threshold configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: Clustering confidence from similarity score and volume. Report both.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ranked clusters with volume, total resolution effort, representative incidents, and Problem linkage state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Clusters representing genuinely distinct incidents with similar wording.

rules.title: P1 and major incidents with no Problem raised
rules.whatItMeans: P1 and major incidents have been closed with no Problem raised.
rules.whyItMatters: The highest-impact incidents are the ones least analysed. Each unanalysed major incident is a guaranteed repeat with no accumulated understanding.
rules.sourceTables: P1 and major incident records, Problem linkage
rules.detectionLogic: P1 and major incidents closed with no linked Problem
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage.
rules.evidenceToShow: Incident list with duration, affected services, business impact, and Problem linkage state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Cause established during the incident and documented.

rules.title: Problem records created but never progressed past initial state
rules.whatItMeans: Problem records are created and never progressed past their initial state.
rules.whyItMatters: The process is adopted in form and not in substance. Creating a Problem becomes a closure ritual for the incident rather than the start of analysis.
rules.sourceTables: problem state, creation date, state change audit
rules.detectionLogic: Problems in the initial state beyond age threshold with no state change
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 30 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on state and audit history.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem list with age, creating group, linked incident count, and absence of state change.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Problems deliberately parked pending a vendor.

rules.title: Percentage of incident volume attributable to known problems
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of incident volume attributable to known problems.
rules.whyItMatters: The value measure for Problem management. A high number with open Problems means known causes are still generating cost; a high number with closed Problems means the fixes did not work.
rules.sourceTables: incident linkage to Problem and Known Error, incident volume
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(incidents linked to a Problem) / COUNT(incidents) in the window, split by Problem state
rules.threshold: Report by Problem state; no single threshold
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio split by open and closed Problems, the top Problems by attributable incident volume, and the effort each represents.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Linkage practice inconsistent, understating the true attribution.
rules.crossDomainLink: The business case for Problem management

rules.title: Top ten incident clusters by short-description similarity with no Problem
rules.whatItMeans: The top incident clusters by short-description similarity have no corresponding Problem.
rules.whyItMatters: The specific, ranked version of ITSM-054. This is the list to put in front of a Problem manager, because each entry carries a volume and an effort number.
rules.sourceTables: incident short_description clustering, resolution effort, Problem linkage
rules.detectionLogic: Top N clusters by volume with no Problem link, ranked by aggregate resolution effort
rules.threshold: N default 10; effort derived from resolution time
rules.confidenceBasis: Clustering confidence from similarity and volume, stated per cluster.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ranked clusters with volume, aggregate effort, representative incidents, the groups resolving them, and the close codes used.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Clusters diluted by ITSM-023 template pasting. Report that finding alongside.
rules.crossDomainLink: The Problem management backlog, ranked by value

rules.title: Problem raised only by one group (process not adopted estate-wide)
rules.whatItMeans: Problem records are raised by only one group, indicating the process is not adopted across the estate.
rules.whyItMatters: One team practises Problem management and the rest do not. The measured Problem ratio looks better than reality because one group carries it.
rules.sourceTables: problem creation by group, incident volume by group
rules.detectionLogic: Problem creation distribution by group, against incident volume distribution
rules.threshold: Flag where Problem creation concentration far exceeds incident concentration
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the distributions.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem creation by group, incident volume by group, and the ratio per group showing the adoption gap.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Centralised Problem function by design.
rules.crossDomainLink: Adoption gap hidden by aggregate metrics

rules.title: Problem records with no linked incidents
rules.whatItMeans: Problem records exist with no linked incidents.
rules.whyItMatters: Either the linkage is not being done, in which case ITSM-057 understates attribution, or the Problem was raised speculatively with no evidence behind it.
rules.sourceTables: problem records, incident linkage
rules.detectionLogic: Problems with zero linked incidents
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report by state
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage count.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem list with state, age, creating group, and the incident clusters that match their description.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Proactive Problems raised from monitoring or trend analysis rather than incidents.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 1 where matching incidents can be identified, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.title: Problems open beyond age threshold with no state change
rules.whatItMeans: Problems are open beyond an age threshold with no state change.
rules.whyItMatters: Analysis stalled. The linked incidents continue to occur while the Problem sits, so the cost continues to accrue with no offsetting progress.
rules.sourceTables: problem state audit history, age
rules.detectionLogic: Open Problems with no state change beyond age threshold
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 90 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on audit history.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem list with age, last state change, owner, linked incident count, and incident volume accrued since the Problem opened.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Problems awaiting a vendor fix with documented tracking.

rules.title: Root cause field empty on closed Problems
rules.whatItMeans: The root cause field is empty on closed Problems.
rules.whyItMatters: The Problem was closed without establishing why. Nothing was learned, the Known Error cannot be written, and the same cause will not be recognised next time.
rules.sourceTables: problem cause_notes or root cause field, closed Problems
rules.detectionLogic: Closed Problems with empty root cause
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by group and close code, the linked incident volume for each, and the post-closure incident trend.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Problems closed as duplicates or cancelled.

rules.title: Workaround empty on Problems with open linked incidents
rules.whatItMeans: The workaround field is empty on Problems that have open linked incidents.
rules.whyItMatters: Service desk agents have no interim guidance while the permanent fix is developed. Every linked incident is resolved from scratch.
rules.sourceTables: problem workaround field, linked incident state
rules.detectionLogic: Problems with open linked incidents and empty workaround
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state and linkage.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem list with open incident count, workaround state, and the average resolution time for linked incidents.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: No workaround genuinely exists.
rules.crossDomainLink: Direct cost in repeated resolution effort

rules.title: Problem closed with no permanent fix and no accepted-risk decision
rules.whatItMeans: A Problem is closed with no permanent fix recorded and no documented accepted-risk decision.
rules.whyItMatters: Closed without resolution and without a decision to accept it. The record says the Problem is dealt with and nothing changed.
rules.sourceTables: problem closure, fix and known error linkage, accepted risk field
rules.detectionLogic: Closed Problems with no linked Change, no Known Error, and no accepted-risk record
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage and field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem list, closure code, linked artefacts, and the post-closure incident volume for each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Fix implemented outside ServiceNow with evidence.

rules.title: Problem with no assigned owner, or owner inactive
rules.whatItMeans: A Problem has no assigned owner, or the owner is an inactive user.
rules.whyItMatters: Nobody is progressing it. The Problem exists as a record with no path to resolution.
rules.sourceTables: problem assigned_to and assignment_group, sys_user.active, group membership
rules.detectionLogic: Problems with empty owner, or owner resolving to an inactive user or empty group
rules.threshold: Active membership resolved live
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — resolves to an active person or does not.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem list with owner state, age, linked incident count, and last activity.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Owner deactivated within a grace period with reassignment pending.

rules.title: Known Error records not published to knowledge
rules.whatItMeans: Known Error records are not published to the knowledge base.
rules.whyItMatters: The analysis exists and cannot be consumed. Agents resolving linked incidents cannot find the workaround that was written specifically for them.
rules.sourceTables: Known Error records, kb_knowledge linkage and publication state
rules.detectionLogic: Known Errors with no published knowledge article, or with an article in draft
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage and publication state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Known Error list, article state, linked incident volume, and article view counts where published.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Knowledge published in a separate system.

rules.title: Problem not linked to a CI or service
rules.whatItMeans: A Problem is not linked to a CI or a service.
rules.whyItMatters: The Problem cannot be aggregated by infrastructure or service. Recurring problems on the same CI are invisible as a pattern.
rules.sourceTables: problem cmdb_ci and business_service fields
rules.detectionLogic: Problems with both CI and service references empty
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem list, linked incident CI distribution, and the CI the incidents point at.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Problems concerning process rather than technology.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 1 where the linked incidents resolve the CI, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.title: Problem tasks created but never completed
rules.whatItMeans: Problem tasks are created and never completed.
rules.whyItMatters: The investigation was broken into steps and the steps were not done. The Problem appears active and is not progressing.
rules.sourceTables: Problem task records, state and age
rules.detectionLogic: Open Problem tasks beyond age threshold
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 60 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on age arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Task list with age, assignee, parent Problem, and the parent's state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Tasks deliberately sequenced with later start dates.

rules.title: Problem closed while linked incidents remain open
rules.whatItMeans: A Problem is closed while its linked incidents remain open.
rules.whyItMatters: The cause is declared resolved while the symptoms are still live. Either the closure is premature or the incidents should have been closed with it.
rules.sourceTables: problem state, linked incident states
rules.detectionLogic: Closed Problems with one or more open linked incidents
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on state check.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem, closure date and code, the open linked incidents with their ages, and their assignment groups.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Incidents legitimately open for a separate reason.

rules.title: Root cause text below meaningful length or restating the symptom
rules.whatItMeans: Root cause text is below a meaningful length, or restates the symptom rather than the cause.
rules.whyItMatters: Passes any mandatory-field check while carrying no analysis. The Known Error written from it will be useless.
rules.sourceTables: problem root cause text length, similarity to the Problem description
rules.detectionLogic: Closed Problems with root cause below length threshold, or similarity to description above threshold
rules.threshold: Length threshold default 40 characters; similarity threshold 0.85
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on length. 90% on the similarity check.
rules.evidenceToShow: Sample records with description and root cause, count by group, and the length distribution.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely simple causes stated concisely.

rules.title: Problem with no linked Change where a fix was clearly required
rules.whatItMeans: A Problem has no linked Change where the root cause clearly required one.
rules.whyItMatters: The cause was identified, the fix required a change, and no change exists. Either the fix was implemented without change control, which is ITSM-106, or it was never implemented.
rules.sourceTables: problem records with root cause established, Change linkage, root cause classification
rules.detectionLogic: Closed Problems with a root cause indicating a configuration or code fix, and no linked Change
rules.threshold: Root cause classification from close code and text pattern
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — the inference that a change was required is derived from the root cause classification.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem, root cause, absence of Change linkage, and any unauthorised change detected on the related CI in the window.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Fix applied through a standard change not linked back.

rules.title: Problem state regressing repeatedly
rules.whatItMeans: A Problem state regresses repeatedly, moving backward through the workflow more than once.
rules.whyItMatters: Analysis is being reopened repeatedly, which usually means the root cause was declared prematurely each time.
rules.sourceTables: problem state audit history, backward transitions
rules.detectionLogic: Problems with more than N backward state transitions
rules.threshold: Default 2 backward transitions
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on audit history.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem, its state timeline, the backward transitions with users and dates, and the linked incident volume across the period.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate iterative investigation.

rules.title: Problem priority not aligned to the aggregate impact of linked incidents
rules.whatItMeans: Problem priority is not aligned to the aggregate impact of its linked incidents.
rules.whyItMatters: A Problem generating a thousand incidents sits at low priority while one generating five sits high. Problem prioritisation is disconnected from the cost it represents.
rules.sourceTables: problem priority, linked incident volume and priority distribution
rules.detectionLogic: Problems whose priority is inconsistent with their linked incident aggregate volume and priority
rules.threshold: Alignment matrix configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — the alignment expectation is encoded in configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem, its priority, linked incident volume and priority spread, and the aggregate resolution effort.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Priority deliberately set on fix complexity rather than incident volume.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 1 where realignment is unambiguous, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.title: Incident volume for a resolved Problem not declining post-closure (fix ineffective)
rules.whatItMeans: Incident volume for a resolved Problem has not declined after closure.
rules.whyItMatters: The fix did not work and nobody checked. The Problem is closed, the metric improved, and the cost continues unchanged. This is the only rule in the group that measures outcome rather than process.
rules.sourceTables: problem closure dates, linked incident volume before and after closure
rules.detectionLogic: Linked incident rate in the N days after closure compared against the N days before
rules.threshold: Window default 90 days either side. Flag where the decline is below threshold.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on volume comparison. Requires sufficient post-closure window; state it.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem, closure date, incident volume trend before and after, and the permanent fix recorded.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Insufficient time since closure. Do not evaluate before the full window has elapsed.
rules.crossDomainLink: The outcome measure for Problem management

rules.title: Problem recurrence — same root cause appearing in multiple Problem records
rules.whatItMeans: The same root cause appears across multiple separate Problem records.
rules.whyItMatters: The cause was identified more than once and resolved more than once, or not at all. Indicates either duplicate Problem creation or a fix that repeatedly fails.
rules.sourceTables: problem root cause text clustering across records
rules.detectionLogic: Problem clusters by root cause similarity above threshold
rules.threshold: Similarity threshold default 0.8, minimum cluster size 2
rules.confidenceBasis: Clustering confidence from similarity score. Report per cluster.
rules.evidenceToShow: The cluster, each Problem with its dates, closure state, permanent fix, and linked incident volume.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely similar but distinct causes on different systems.

rules.title: Known Error articles with no views or no linkage from incidents
rules.whatItMeans: Known Error articles have no views, or no linkage from incidents.
rules.whyItMatters: The knowledge exists and is not reaching agents. Either search is not surfacing it or the suggestion mechanism is not configured, which is ITSM-015.
rules.sourceTables: kb_knowledge view counts, incident-to-article linkage, Known Error records
rules.detectionLogic: Known Error articles with zero views or zero incident linkage in the window
rules.threshold: Window default 90 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on view and linkage counts.
rules.evidenceToShow: Article list with views, linkage count, the incident volume that matched their topic, and the knowledge suggestion configuration state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Articles recently published with insufficient elapsed time.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 for the suggestion configuration, Lane 3 for content

rules.title: Average time from incident cluster emergence to Problem creation
rules.whatItMeans: The average time from incident cluster emergence to Problem creation.
rules.whyItMatters: Measures how long the organisation absorbs a recurring cost before recognising it. Every day in that interval is repeated resolution effort.
rules.sourceTables: incident cluster first occurrence, linked Problem creation date
rules.detectionLogic: Mean and distribution of (Problem created - cluster first occurrence) across linked clusters
rules.threshold: Report distribution, not a single threshold
rules.confidenceBasis: Cluster emergence date confidence from clustering quality.
rules.evidenceToShow: Distribution with the longest cases, the incident volume accrued during each interval, and the effort that represents.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Clusters whose emergence is ambiguous.

rules.title: Permanent fix implemented but no validation recorded
rules.whatItMeans: A permanent fix is recorded as implemented with no validation recorded.
rules.whyItMatters: Nobody confirmed the fix worked. Combined with ITSM-074, this is how ineffective fixes survive as closed Problems.
rules.sourceTables: problem fix records, validation fields, linked Change closure
rules.detectionLogic: Problems with a permanent fix recorded and no validation entry or post-implementation review
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field and linkage state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Problem, fix record, absence of validation, and the post-closure incident trend.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Validation recorded in the linked Change instead.

rules.title: Problems closed as "cannot reproduce" above threshold
rules.whatItMeans: Problems closed as 'cannot reproduce' exceed a threshold share.
rules.whyItMatters: Sometimes legitimate, often a closure of convenience. A high rate concentrated in one group is a behavioural signal rather than a technical one.
rules.sourceTables: problem close codes, distribution by group
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(Problems closed as cannot reproduce) / COUNT(closed Problems), by group
rules.threshold: Default threshold 20%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio by group, the linked incident volume for those Problems, and the post-closure incident trend.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely intermittent issues.

rules.title: Standard change catalogue empty or unused — everything routed as Normal
rules.whatItMeans: The standard change catalogue is empty or unused, so all work routes as Normal change.
rules.whyItMatters: Low-risk repeatable work carries full CAB overhead. Two consequences: the CAB spends its time on routine work rather than risk, and engineers route around the process because it is disproportionate.
rules.sourceTables: Standard change template records, change type distribution
rules.detectionLogic: Standard change template count and usage against total change volume
rules.threshold: Default threshold 20% of changes as standard for a mature estate
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the distribution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change type distribution, standard template count and usage, and the Normal changes with repeated identical descriptions that are standard-change candidates.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Estate genuinely has no repeatable change patterns.
rules.crossDomainLink: Drives CAB overload and process avoidance

rules.title: Approval routing with no defined approver group for a change type
rules.whatItMeans: A change type has no defined approver group in its approval routing.
rules.whyItMatters: Changes of that type either bypass approval or hang indefinitely. Both outcomes are control failures, and which one occurs depends on workflow configuration nobody has checked.
rules.sourceTables: Change approval workflow configuration by type, approver group assignment
rules.detectionLogic: Change types with volume but no configured approver group
rules.threshold: Any type with non-zero volume
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change type, volume, approval configuration state, and the actual approval records for changes of that type.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Type deliberately auto-approved with documented rationale.

rules.title: CAB not configured, or CAB meeting workflow unused
rules.whatItMeans: CAB is not configured, or the CAB meeting workflow exists and is unused.
rules.whyItMatters: There is no forum where change risk is collectively assessed. Approval becomes individual and asynchronous, which removes the cross-domain conflict detection that a CAB exists to provide.
rules.sourceTables: CAB configuration, CAB meeting records, change agenda linkage
rules.detectionLogic: CAB configuration absent, or zero CAB meeting records in the window despite change volume
rules.threshold: Window default 90 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration and record count.
rules.evidenceToShow: CAB configuration state, meeting record count, change volume, and the approval mechanism actually in use.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: CAB conducted outside ServiceNow with documented evidence.

rules.title: Risk assessment not configured, or risk always computed as the same value
rules.whatItMeans: Risk assessment is not configured, or risk is computed as the same value for every change.
rules.whyItMatters: Risk stops differentiating. Every change carries the same assessment, so approval routing and scrutiny cannot vary by actual risk. Usually the risk questionnaire exists and nobody answers it.
rules.sourceTables: Change risk field distribution, risk assessment configuration and questionnaire completion
rules.detectionLogic: Risk value distribution; flag where one value exceeds threshold share, or where risk assessment is unconfigured
rules.threshold: Default 80% in one risk value
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the distribution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Risk distribution, the assessment configuration, questionnaire completion rate, and the correlation between assigned risk and actual change failure rate.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely homogeneous change portfolio.

rules.title: No conflict detection configured
rules.whatItMeans: No change conflict detection is configured.
rules.whyItMatters: Two changes can be approved for the same CI in the same window with nothing detecting the collision. The most common cause of change-induced incidents is two changes nobody knew about each other.
rules.sourceTables: Conflict detection configuration, change schedule overlap analysis
rules.detectionLogic: Conflict detection unconfigured, or configured with zero detections despite overlapping changes existing
rules.threshold: Report both cases; the second is ITSM-138
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Configuration state, the overlapping changes that existed and were not detected, and the incidents that followed them.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Conflict managed manually through the CAB with evidence.

rules.title: Blackout and maintenance windows not defined
rules.whatItMeans: Blackout and maintenance windows are not defined.
rules.whyItMatters: There is no mechanism to prevent change during periods when change should not happen. Quarter-end, peak trading, regulatory reporting windows are all unprotected.
rules.sourceTables: cmn_schedule blackout and maintenance window definitions, change activity distribution
rules.detectionLogic: Absence of blackout or maintenance window definitions where change volume exists
rules.threshold: Any absence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Schedule configuration state, change volume distribution by date, and any change activity during known sensitive periods.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Windows managed through a separate calendar with evidence.

rules.title: Emergency change path with the same approval requirements as Normal (so it gets bypassed)
rules.whatItMeans: The emergency change path carries the same approval burden as a Normal change.
rules.whyItMatters: The emergency path exists to move fast under control. If it is no faster, it gets bypassed entirely and emergency work happens with no record at all, which is worse than either alternative.
rules.sourceTables: Change type approval configuration, approval step counts and turnaround by type
rules.detectionLogic: Emergency change approval step count and turnaround compared against Normal
rules.threshold: Flag where emergency approval burden is not materially lighter
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Approval configuration by type, step counts, actual turnaround distribution, and the unauthorised change rate for comparison.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate design with a documented fast-track mechanism elsewhere.

rules.title: Change model states allowing closure without implementation evidence
rules.whatItMeans: The change model permits closure without any implementation evidence recorded.
rules.whyItMatters: Changes close as Successful with nothing to show they were implemented. Audit has no evidence trail, and post-implementation review has nothing to review.
rules.sourceTables: Change state model, closure requirements, close notes and implementation evidence population
rules.detectionLogic: Change models allowing closure with empty close notes and no implementation evidence fields required
rules.threshold: Any model permitting evidenceless closure
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on model configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Model configuration, closure requirements, and the proportion of closed changes with no implementation evidence.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Evidence captured in an external deployment system with linkage.

rules.title: Approval delegation configured to inactive users
rules.whatItMeans: Approval delegation is configured to inactive users.
rules.whyItMatters: Delegated approvals route to nobody. Changes hang, and the workaround is usually to bypass approval, which becomes ITSM-106.
rules.sourceTables: Approval delegation configuration, sys_user.active
rules.detectionLogic: Active delegations whose delegate resolves to an inactive user
rules.threshold: Active delegation records only
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — resolves to an active user or does not.
rules.evidenceToShow: Delegation record, delegator, delegate state, and the approvals currently hanging on it.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Delegate deactivated within a grace period.

rules.title: Standard change templates with no expiry or review date
rules.whatItMeans: Standard change templates have no expiry or review date.
rules.whyItMatters: A standard change is pre-approved because the risk was assessed once. Without review, that assessment ages indefinitely while the environment changes underneath it.
rules.sourceTables: Standard change template records, expiry and review date fields
rules.detectionLogic: Standard templates with no expiry or review date, or past review date
rules.threshold: Review period from policy; default 12 months
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Template list with creation date, last review, usage volume, and the change success rate for changes raised from each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Templates under a documented external review cycle.
rules.crossDomainLink: Pre-approval based on an ageing assessment

rules.title: Risk matrix fields not mandatory
rules.whatItMeans: Risk matrix input fields are not mandatory.
rules.whyItMatters: Risk can be computed from an incomplete assessment, or defaulted. Produces ITSM-083 as a downstream effect.
rules.sourceTables: Risk assessment field mandatory configuration, field population rates
rules.detectionLogic: Risk matrix input fields with no mandatory enforcement and population rate below threshold
rules.threshold: Population threshold default 80%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration and population.
rules.evidenceToShow: Field list, mandatory state, population rate, and the resulting risk value distribution.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Risk assessed through a questionnaire with its own enforcement.

rules.title: Change types customised without corresponding approval logic
rules.whatItMeans: Custom change types have been created without corresponding approval logic.
rules.whyItMatters: The type exists, changes are raised against it, and no approval workflow covers it. A control gap created by configuration rather than by bypass.
rules.sourceTables: Change type choices vs OOB set, approval workflow coverage by type
rules.detectionLogic: Custom change types with volume and no matching approval workflow condition
rules.threshold: Any custom type with non-zero volume
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on workflow condition coverage.
rules.evidenceToShow: Custom type, volume, approval workflow coverage, and the actual approval records for changes of that type.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Type covered by a general workflow condition.

rules.title: No post-implementation review step for high-risk changes
rules.whatItMeans: There is no post-implementation review step configured for high-risk changes.
rules.whyItMatters: High-risk changes are implemented and never reviewed. Whether they achieved their objective, and what they broke, is never established.
rules.sourceTables: Change model PIR configuration by risk band, PIR record existence
rules.detectionLogic: High-risk change types with no PIR step configured, or zero PIR records for high-risk changes
rules.threshold: Risk bands configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration and record count.
rules.evidenceToShow: Configuration state by risk band, high-risk change volume, PIR record count, and the incident rate following high-risk changes.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: PIR conducted through a separate process.

rules.title: Change calendar not published or not consumed
rules.whatItMeans: The change calendar is not published, or is published and not consumed.
rules.whyItMatters: Teams cannot see what else is happening. Conflict detection catches technical collisions; the calendar catches the human ones, and without it nobody knows a related change is in flight.
rules.sourceTables: Change calendar configuration and publication, calendar view access logs where available
rules.detectionLogic: Calendar unconfigured or unpublished, or published with negligible access
rules.threshold: Access threshold where log data is available
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration. Consumption depends on access log availability.
rules.evidenceToShow: Calendar configuration state, publication, access volume, and the change volume it would cover.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Calendar consumed through an exported feed.

rules.title: Percentage of changes with no CI and no service reference
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of changes referencing neither a CI nor a service.
rules.whyItMatters: Conflict detection, risk assessment and impact analysis all key off the CI reference. Without it, none of them can run, so the change is approved on narrative alone.
rules.sourceTables: change_request.cmdb_ci and business_service, change volume
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(changes with both fields empty) / COUNT(changes) in the window
rules.threshold: Default threshold 30%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio trend, distribution by type and group, and the conflict detection results for changes with and without CI references.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Change types where no CI is meaningful, such as process or documentation changes.
rules.crossDomainLink: Makes ITSM-084 and ITSM-138 structurally impossible

rules.title: Change referencing a retired or non-existent CI
rules.whatItMeans: A change references a CI that is retired or does not exist.
rules.whyItMatters: The change targets infrastructure that officially does not exist. Conflict detection and impact analysis traverse from a dead record and return nothing.
rules.sourceTables: change_request.cmdb_ci, cmdb_ci existence and lifecycle
rules.detectionLogic: Changes referencing a CI sys_id with no record, or a CI in a retired state
rules.threshold: Report the two cases separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on existence and state check.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change list, the referenced CI and its state, and the live CI the change probably concerns.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Change raised specifically to complete a decommission.

rules.title: Implementation plan empty
rules.whatItMeans: The implementation plan is empty.
rules.whyItMatters: The approver is approving an unspecified action. There is no basis on which to assess risk, and no record of what was supposed to happen if it goes wrong.
rules.sourceTables: change_request implementation plan field
rules.detectionLogic: Approved or closed changes with empty implementation plan
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report by type and risk band
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by type, risk band and group, with the approval records showing what was approved without a plan.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Standard changes where the template carries the plan.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 — mandatory enforcement at the approval state

rules.title: Backout plan empty
rules.whatItMeans: The backout plan is empty.
rules.whyItMatters: When the change fails, there is no documented way back. The recovery is improvised during an incident, which is the worst possible time to design it.
rules.sourceTables: change_request backout plan field
rules.detectionLogic: Approved or closed changes with empty backout plan
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; escalate for high-risk and production changes
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by risk band and type, the failed changes among them, and the recovery time for those failures.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Standard changes where the template carries the backout.

rules.title: Test plan empty on high-risk changes
rules.whatItMeans: The test plan is empty on high-risk changes.
rules.whyItMatters: High-risk change proceeding with no defined verification. Whether it worked is established by whether something breaks.
rules.sourceTables: change_request test plan field, risk band
rules.detectionLogic: High-risk changes with empty test plan
rules.threshold: Risk bands configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by risk band and group, the change success rate for these versus those with test plans.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Testing evidenced in a linked external record.
rules.crossDomainLink: No defined verification on the riskiest work

rules.title: Risk and impact fields unpopulated
rules.whatItMeans: Risk and impact fields are unpopulated.
rules.whyItMatters: The change carries no assessment at all. Approval routing that keys off risk cannot function, so it defaults, usually to the lightest path.
rules.sourceTables: change_request risk and impact fields
rules.detectionLogic: Changes with risk or impact unpopulated at approval
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by type and group, the approval path taken for each, and the change success rate.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Types where risk is inherited from the template.
rules.crossDomainLink: Approval routing defaults to the lightest path

rules.title: Planned start and end dates absent or in the past at approval
rules.whatItMeans: Planned start and end dates are absent, or are in the past at the point of approval.
rules.whyItMatters: A change with no window cannot be conflict-checked, cannot be calendared, and cannot be verified as implemented within its approval. Past dates at approval indicate retrospective raising.
rules.sourceTables: change_request planned start and end dates, approval timestamps
rules.detectionLogic: Changes with empty planned dates at approval, or planned start earlier than approval date
rules.threshold: Report the two cases separately; the second feeds ITSM-108
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on date arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change list with planned dates, approval date, actual implementation date, and the gap.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Emergency changes approved after the fact under a documented emergency process.
rules.crossDomainLink: Feeds ITSM-108 and blocks conflict detection

rules.title: Assignment group with zero active members
rules.whatItMeans: A change is assigned to a group with zero active members.
rules.whyItMatters: The implementation has no owner. The change sits in a queue nobody sees until the planned window passes.
rules.sourceTables: change_request.assignment_group, sys_user_grmember, sys_user.active
rules.detectionLogic: Open changes whose assignment group resolves to zero active members
rules.threshold: Active membership resolved live
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — resolves to a person or does not.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change count by group, their planned windows, risk bands, and the empty groups with last membership change date.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Group emptied with reassignment in progress.
rules.crossDomainLink: Cross-links to CMDB-102 and Data Quality Q2

rules.title: Justification or business reason empty
rules.whatItMeans: The justification or business reason field is empty.
rules.whyItMatters: The change has no recorded purpose. Audit cannot establish why it was made, and post-implementation review cannot assess whether it achieved anything.
rules.sourceTables: change_request justification or business reason field
rules.detectionLogic: Approved or closed changes with empty justification
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by type, group and risk band, with the approval records.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Justification carried in the linked incident or problem.

rules.title: Change closed with no close code or close notes
rules.whatItMeans: A change is closed with no close code or close notes.
rules.whyItMatters: Whether the change succeeded is unrecorded. The change success rate, which is the primary quality measure for the process, is computed over incomplete data.
rules.sourceTables: change_request close_code and close_notes on closed changes
rules.detectionLogic: Closed changes with empty close code or close notes
rules.threshold: Report the two cases separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by type and group, and the change success rate computed with and without these records.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Closure via an automated integration not populating the fields.

rules.title: Backout plan text identical across many changes (template pasting)
rules.whatItMeans: Backout plan text is identical across a large number of changes.
rules.whyItMatters: Template pasting. The field is populated, the control appears satisfied, and no change has a backout plan specific to what it is actually doing.
rules.sourceTables: change_request backout plan text frequency distribution
rules.detectionLogic: Backout plan values appearing above a volume threshold, normalised
rules.threshold: Volume threshold configurable relative to change volume
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on frequency. The template-pasting interpretation is inferred.
rules.evidenceToShow: Repeated text with volume, the groups producing it, and the change types involved.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimately identical backout for a genuinely repeatable standard change.

rules.title: Affected CI list containing a single CI where the change clearly spans more
rules.whatItMeans: The affected CI list contains a single CI where the change clearly spans more.
rules.whyItMatters: Under-declared scope. Conflict detection and impact analysis run against a fraction of what the change touches, so both return falsely reassuring results.
rules.sourceTables: change_request affected CI list, CI relationship traversal from the primary CI
rules.detectionLogic: Changes with a single affected CI whose description or type indicates broader scope, or whose primary CI has dependent CIs not declared
rules.threshold: Scope inference from change type and CI relationship depth
rules.confidenceBasis: 80% — scope inference is the weakest rule in this group. Report with the relationship evidence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, declared CI, the dependent CIs not declared, and the conflict detection result with and without them.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Change genuinely scoped to one CI.

rules.title: Unauthorised change rate — CI modified with no corresponding approved change
rules.whatItMeans: CIs have been modified with no corresponding approved change record.
rules.whyItMatters: The change control process was bypassed. For a regulated entity this is the most consequential finding in the ITSM catalogue, because it is a direct audit exception rather than a quality observation.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci and configuration object audit history, change_request records and windows, CI-to-change correlation
rules.detectionLogic: Configuration modifications on change-controlled objects with no approved change covering the object and timestamp
rules.threshold: Scope to change-controlled object classes; correlation window configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — attribution depends on audit completeness and on change records carrying accurate CI references. Where ITSM-094 is high, this rule understates.
rules.evidenceToShow: The modification with object, timestamp and user, the absence of a covering change, and the approved changes in the window for comparison.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Change raised without a CI reference, so the correlation fails. Report ITSM-094 alongside and state the understatement.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — this is an audit finding, not a data fix
rules.crossDomainLink: The headline control integrity finding; route to audit

rules.title: Emergency change ratio above threshold (emergency used to bypass control)
rules.whatItMeans: The emergency change ratio exceeds threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: Emergency exists to handle genuine urgency. A high ratio means it is being used to avoid the Normal approval path, which converts a control into a formality.
rules.sourceTables: change_request type distribution, emergency change volume
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(emergency changes) / COUNT(all changes), overall and by group and approver
rules.threshold: Default threshold 10%. Escalate above 25%.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio overall, by group and by approver, with the emergency justifications and the approval turnaround for each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: A period of genuine operational crisis.
rules.crossDomainLink: Control integrity; concentration by approver is the strongest signal

rules.title: Retrospective change rate — changes raised after implementation
rules.whatItMeans: Changes are being raised after they have already been implemented.
rules.whyItMatters: The record is created to satisfy the process rather than to control the work. Approval is retrospective and therefore meaningless as a control.
rules.sourceTables: change_request creation timestamp, planned and actual start, CI modification timestamps
rules.detectionLogic: Changes whose creation or approval timestamp postdates the actual implementation evidence
rules.threshold: Correlation against CI audit where available; otherwise against actual start field
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% where CI audit corroborates. 80% where only the actual start field is available.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, creation and approval timestamps, actual implementation evidence and its timestamp, and the gap.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Emergency changes raised retrospectively under a documented emergency process.

rules.title: Self-approval — requester and approver the same person
rules.whatItMeans: The requester and the approver on a change are the same person.
rules.whyItMatters: A segregation of duties failure. One person authorised their own work. In a regulated entity this is an audit exception regardless of whether the change was appropriate.
rules.sourceTables: change_request requested_by, approval records approver
rules.detectionLogic: Changes where an approval record's approver equals the requester
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — direct comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, requester, approver, approval timestamp, risk band, and the affected CIs.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Documented single-person authority for a defined low-risk category with compensating controls.
rules.crossDomainLink: Segregation of duties failure; route to audit

rules.title: Approval granted outside the approver's authority level
rules.whatItMeans: Approval was granted by someone outside the authority level required for that change's risk band.
rules.whyItMatters: The approval exists and was not valid. Subtler than self-approval and equally consequential, because the control appears satisfied on the record.
rules.sourceTables: Approval records, approver role and authority configuration, change risk band
rules.detectionLogic: Approvals where the approver's authority level is below that required for the change risk band
rules.threshold: Authority matrix from the customer's own delegation policy
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% where an authority matrix exists. Where none exists, report that absence instead.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, risk band, required authority, the approver and their actual authority, and the approval record.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Delegated authority not reflected in the role configuration.
rules.crossDomainLink: Control integrity; requires the authority matrix to detect

rules.title: Change implemented outside its approved window
rules.whatItMeans: A change was implemented outside its approved window.
rules.whyItMatters: What was approved and what happened are different. Conflict detection and calendar protection were both computed against the approved window and do not apply to the actual one.
rules.sourceTables: change_request planned start and end, actual start and end, or CI modification timestamps
rules.detectionLogic: Changes whose actual implementation falls outside the approved planned window beyond tolerance
rules.threshold: Tolerance configurable, default 1 hour
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% where actual timestamps are populated; 90% where inferred from CI audit.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, approved window, actual implementation window, the deviation, and any conflicting change in the actual window.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Window extended through a documented approval amendment.
rules.crossDomainLink: Invalidates conflict detection and calendar protection

rules.title: Change implemented during a blackout period
rules.whatItMeans: A change was implemented during a defined blackout period.
rules.whyItMatters: The blackout existed to protect a period the business identified as sensitive, and it was crossed. The most directly reportable control breach in the change catalogue.
rules.sourceTables: change_request implementation timestamps, cmn_schedule blackout definitions
rules.detectionLogic: Changes whose implementation window intersects a defined blackout period
rules.threshold: Requires blackout windows to be defined; report ITSM-085 where they are not
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on window intersection where blackouts are defined.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, implementation window, the blackout period it crossed, the approver, and any override justification.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Documented blackout exception approved in advance.

rules.title: Change success rate below threshold
rules.whatItMeans: The change success rate is below threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: The primary quality measure for change management. Only meaningful alongside ITSM-103 and ITSM-115, because closure codes are frequently inaccurate.
rules.sourceTables: change_request close codes, closed change volume
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(changes closed successful) / COUNT(closed changes), by type, risk band and group
rules.threshold: Default threshold 90%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio, conditional on close code accuracy. Report ITSM-103 and ITSM-115 alongside.
rules.evidenceToShow: Success rate by type, risk band and group, with the trend and the incident rate following changes.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Close codes unreliable, overstating success. Report the qualifying findings.
rules.crossDomainLink: Requires ITSM-103 and ITSM-115 to interpret

rules.title: Failed change rate with no corresponding backout executed
rules.whatItMeans: Changes failed with no corresponding backout executed.
rules.whyItMatters: The change failed and the environment was left in the failed state. Either the backout plan was not usable or nobody executed it, and in both cases the recovery was improvised.
rules.sourceTables: change_request close codes indicating failure, backout execution records or task closure
rules.detectionLogic: Failed changes with no backout task completed or backout evidence recorded
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on closure and task state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Failed change list, backout plan content, backout execution evidence, and the incidents raised following each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Backout not required because the change did not reach a state needing reversal.

rules.title: Changes closed as Successful with a linked incident created within the window
rules.whatItMeans: Changes closed as Successful have a linked incident created within the post-implementation window.
rules.whyItMatters: The change is recorded as successful and caused an incident. The success rate is overstated by exactly this population, which is why ITSM-113 cannot be read alone.
rules.sourceTables: change_request closure, incident creation timestamps and CI correlation, post-implementation window
rules.detectionLogic: Successful changes with an incident on the same or dependent CI within the window after implementation
rules.threshold: Window default 72 hours. CI correlation includes dependent CIs where relationships exist.
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — correlation by CI and timing is strong but circumstantial without an explicit link.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, closure code, the correlated incident with its timing and CI, and the corrected success rate.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Coincidental incident unrelated to the change.

rules.title: Approval turnaround near-zero (rubber-stamping)
rules.whatItMeans: Approval turnaround is near zero — approvals granted within seconds or minutes of request.
rules.whyItMatters: Nobody read it. The approval control is executing and producing no scrutiny, which is indistinguishable from no control at all from a risk perspective.
rules.sourceTables: Approval records, request and approval timestamps, distribution by approver
rules.detectionLogic: Approvals with turnaround below threshold, grouped by approver and change type
rules.threshold: Default threshold 120 seconds. Report the distribution, not only the outliers.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on timestamp arithmetic. The interpretation is inferred and should be stated as such.
rules.evidenceToShow: Turnaround distribution by approver, the sub-threshold population, the risk bands involved, and each approver's total volume.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Approvals genuinely pre-discussed in a CAB and formalised afterwards.
rules.crossDomainLink: Control integrity; concentration by approver is the signal

rules.title: Standard change used for work that meets Normal change criteria
rules.whatItMeans: Standard change is being used for work that meets Normal change criteria.
rules.whyItMatters: The pre-approval was granted for a defined low-risk activity and is being applied to something else. The scrutiny that the work required was bypassed by template selection.
rules.sourceTables: Standard change template scope, actual change content and affected CIs, risk indicators
rules.detectionLogic: Standard changes whose affected CIs, risk indicators or description fall outside the template scope
rules.threshold: Template scope from the template definition
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — scope comparison depends on template definitions being specific enough to compare against.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change, the template used, its defined scope, the actual scope, and the risk indicators that would have applied under Normal.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Template scope defined broadly and legitimately covering the work.

rules.title: Conflict detected but overridden with no justification
rules.whatItMeans: A conflict was detected and overridden with no justification recorded.
rules.whyItMatters: The control worked, the warning was given, and it was dismissed silently. Nobody can establish why the risk was accepted.
rules.sourceTables: Conflict detection results, override records, justification field
rules.detectionLogic: Detected conflicts with an override and no justification text
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on override and field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Conflict, the changes involved, the override user and timestamp, and any incident that followed.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Justification recorded in work notes rather than the field.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 — make justification mandatory on override

rules.title: Change with no linked incident or problem and no business justification
rules.whatItMeans: A change has no linked incident or problem and no business justification.
rules.whyItMatters: The change has no traceable origin. It was made because someone decided to, with no recorded demand behind it.
rules.sourceTables: change_request incident and problem linkage, justification field
rules.detectionLogic: Changes with no linked incident, no linked problem, and empty justification
rules.threshold: All three absent
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage and field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change list by type and group, with the affected CIs and the approval records.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Proactive maintenance or project work with justification held in a linked project record.

rules.title: Changes repeatedly rescheduled
rules.whatItMeans: Changes are repeatedly rescheduled.
rules.whyItMatters: Each reschedule invalidates the conflict detection and calendar position computed for the prior window. Frequent rescheduling also suggests the planning is not realistic.
rules.sourceTables: change_request planned date audit history, reschedule count
rules.detectionLogic: Changes with more than N planned date changes
rules.threshold: Default 3 reschedules
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on audit history.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change list with reschedule count and timeline, the groups involved, and whether conflict detection was re-run after each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate rescheduling due to external dependency.

rules.title: Approvals by a single approver across a disproportionate share of changes
rules.whatItMeans: A single approver accounts for a disproportionate share of all change approvals.
rules.whyItMatters: Concentration risk and a scrutiny risk. One person cannot meaningfully assess a very high volume, which is usually confirmed by their turnaround distribution.
rules.sourceTables: Approval records by approver, total approval volume
rules.detectionLogic: Approvers holding more than threshold share of total approvals
rules.threshold: Default 25% of total approvals
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on distribution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Approval distribution by approver, the top approvers with volume, and their turnaround distribution for cross-reference against ITSM-116.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: A designated change authority role with a deliberate concentration.
rules.crossDomainLink: Pairs with ITSM-116; concentration plus fast turnaround is the strong finding

rules.title: Change closed without post-implementation review where required
rules.whatItMeans: A change is closed without the post-implementation review that its risk band requires.
rules.whyItMatters: The review requirement exists and is not enforced at closure. High-risk changes complete with no assessment of outcome.
rules.sourceTables: change_request closure, PIR requirement by risk band, PIR record linkage
rules.detectionLogic: Closed changes in risk bands requiring PIR with no linked PIR record
rules.threshold: Risk bands requiring PIR configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on linkage and configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Change list by risk band, PIR requirement, linkage state, and the incident rate following them.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: PIR conducted through a separate process with evidence.
rules.crossDomainLink: No outcome assessment on high-risk change

rules.title: Percentage of P1 incidents preceded by a change on the same CI within the window
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of P1 incidents preceded by a change on the same or a dependent CI within the correlation window.
rules.whyItMatters: The single most useful number in change management. It converts an abstract quality discussion into a measured statement about how much of the worst operational impact is self-inflicted.
rules.sourceTables: P1 incidents with CI references, change_request implementation windows, CI relationship traversal
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(P1 incidents with a preceding change on the same or dependent CI in the window) / COUNT(P1 incidents with a CI reference)
