rules.falsePositiveGuard: Exceptions deliberately propagated to callers that handle them.

rules.title: Overriding an OOB Script Include
rules.whatItMeans: A custom Script Include overrides an out-of-box Script Include.
rules.whyItMatters: Platform logic replaced. Every upgrade improvement to that include is skipped, and the custom version accumulates divergence from the platform.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_include records, OOB inventory, name matching
rules.detectionLogic: Custom includes with the same name as an OOB include
rules.threshold: Name exact match within scope
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — name match within scope is strong evidence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Custom include, the OOB include shadowed, the functional difference, caller count, and skipped update history.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate documented replacement.

rules.title: Synchronous GlideAjax or getReference without callback
rules.whatItMeans: Client scripts use synchronous GlideAjax or getReference without a callback.
rules.whyItMatters: The browser freezes until the server responds. Every form load or field change carries the full server round trip with the UI locked. The most visible performance defect a user experiences.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client script bodies, GlideAjax and getReference call analysis
rules.detectionLogic: Client scripts with getXMLWait, or getReference called without a callback parameter
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — pattern detection of synchronous call forms.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script, the synchronous call, the table and form, the field it fires on, and the form view volume.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Calls in an administrative form with negligible volume.

rules.title: DOM manipulation (document.getElementById, jQuery)
rules.whatItMeans: Client scripts manipulate the DOM directly using document.getElementById or jQuery.
rules.whyItMatters: Bypasses the platform's UI API. Breaks on every UI framework change and on every upgrade, and behaves differently across form views.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client script bodies, DOM access pattern detection
rules.detectionLogic: Client scripts containing direct DOM access or jQuery selectors
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — pattern detection.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script, the DOM access, the table and form, and the UI framework versions it must survive.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legacy scripts on forms scheduled for retirement.
rules.crossDomainLink: Breaks at every UI framework change and upgrade

rules.title: Client script running on load performing server round-trips
rules.whatItMeans: A client script runs on form load and performs server round trips.
rules.whyItMatters: Every form open incurs the round trip. Multiplied by view volume this is a substantial and entirely avoidable load, and the user waits for all of it.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client type and script body, server call detection
rules.detectionLogic: onLoad client scripts containing GlideAjax, GlideRecord or getReference calls
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; rank by form view volume
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — pattern detection.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script, the server calls, the table and form, view volume, and the resulting server call count.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Data genuinely required at load with no alternative.
rules.crossDomainLink: Load cost multiplied by view volume

rules.title: Client script duplicating logic available in a UI Policy
rules.whatItMeans: A client script duplicates logic that a UI Policy could implement declaratively.
rules.whyItMatters: Scripted where configuration would do. Harder to maintain, slower to execute, and invisible to anyone reviewing UI Policies.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client script bodies, UI policy capability mapping
rules.detectionLogic: Client scripts performing only field visibility, mandatory or read-only manipulation
rules.threshold: Operation classification configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — operation classification from script analysis.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script, the operations it performs, the equivalent UI Policy configuration, and the table and form.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Logic with conditions a UI Policy cannot express.

rules.title: Multiple onChange scripts on the same field
rules.whatItMeans: Multiple onChange client scripts fire on the same field.
rules.whyItMatters: Execution order between them is not guaranteed and they may contradict each other. Behaviour becomes inconsistent in ways that are very hard to reproduce.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client field and type, grouping by table and field
rules.detectionLogic: Table and field combinations with more than one active onChange script
rules.threshold: Any occurrence with more than one
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the grouping.
rules.evidenceToShow: Field, the scripts firing on it, their order values where set, and what each does.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Scripts with mutually exclusive conditions.

rules.title: Client script with no condition, running on every form load
rules.whatItMeans: A client script has no condition and runs on every form load.
rules.whyItMatters: Executes regardless of relevance. Individually small, cumulatively significant on forms with many scripts.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client condition field and type
rules.detectionLogic: onLoad client scripts with empty condition
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script list by table and form, form view volume, and the scripts' execution content.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Scripts that genuinely must run on every load.

rules.title: Client script referencing fields not present on the form
rules.whatItMeans: A client script references fields that are not present on the form.
rules.whyItMatters: The reference resolves to nothing. The script either errors in the browser console or silently does nothing, and the intended behaviour is absent.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client script bodies, form layout field lists
rules.detectionLogic: Client script field references absent from the form layouts the script applies to
rules.threshold: Requires form layout introspection
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — field references may be conditional or dot-walked.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script, the referenced field, the form layouts, and the behaviour that does not occur.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Fields present on some views and not others.

rules.title: Client script not compatible with the current UI framework
rules.whatItMeans: Client scripts are not compatible with the current UI framework.
rules.whyItMatters: Written for a prior UI and running, or failing, on the current one. The failure is often partial, which is worse than total because it is not noticed.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client script bodies, deprecated API and framework pattern detection, instance UI configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Client scripts using APIs deprecated or unsupported in the current UI framework
rules.threshold: Deprecated API set per UI framework version
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — depends on the deprecation list for the instance's UI version.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script, the incompatible API, the current UI framework, the forms affected, and the browser error volume where available.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Scripts scoped to a legacy UI still in use.
rules.crossDomainLink: Partial silent failure after UI changes

rules.title: Client-side validation with no matching server-side enforcement
rules.whatItMeans: Client-side validation exists with no matching server-side enforcement.
rules.whyItMatters: Anyone with API, import set or web service access bypasses it entirely. The validation is a UX convenience presented as a control, and in a regulated entity that distinction matters.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script_client validation logic, data policy and business rule server-side equivalents
rules.detectionLogic: Client-side validation rules with no corresponding data policy or server-side business rule on the same field
rules.threshold: Field-level comparison between client validation and server enforcement
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — equivalence detection between client and server logic is inferential.
rules.evidenceToShow: Client validation, the field, the absent server-side enforcement, and the API and import volume writing to that field.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Validation genuinely UX-only with no control intent.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 — data policy as update set

rules.title: UI Policy enforcing mandatory fields with no corresponding Data Policy (API bypass)
rules.whatItMeans: A UI Policy enforces mandatory fields with no corresponding Data Policy.
rules.whyItMatters: The field is mandatory in the browser and nullable through the API, import sets and web services. Every integration writing to that table can create records the UI would have rejected.
rules.sourceTables: UI policy mandatory actions, data policy coverage for the same fields
rules.detectionLogic: UI policy mandatory field actions with no matching data policy rule
rules.threshold: Field-level comparison
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the configuration comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: UI policy, the mandatory fields, absent data policy coverage, and the record count created through API and import with those fields empty.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Field deliberately mandatory only for interactive users.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 — data policy as update set
rules.crossDomainLink: The most common bypassable-control pattern in ServiceNow

rules.title: Conflicting UI Policies on the same field
rules.whatItMeans: Conflicting UI Policies act on the same field.
rules.whyItMatters: One makes it mandatory, another makes it read-only. The outcome depends on execution order, which produces behaviour users describe as random.
rules.sourceTables: UI policy actions grouped by table and field, action conflict detection
rules.detectionLogic: Field-level action sets containing contradictory actions across active policies
rules.threshold: Conflict matrix: mandatory vs read-only, visible vs hidden
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the conflict detection.
rules.evidenceToShow: Field, the conflicting policies, their conditions and order, and the contradictory actions.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Policies with mutually exclusive conditions.

rules.title: Data Policy not applied to import sets or web services where it should be
rules.whatItMeans: Data Policies are not applied to import sets or web services where they should be.
rules.whyItMatters: The data policy exists and is scoped to exclude the paths most likely to introduce bad data. Integrations bypass the validation that interactive users cannot.
rules.sourceTables: Data policy apply-to configuration for import sets and SOAP/REST
rules.detectionLogic: Data policies with import set or web service application disabled
rules.threshold: Any occurrence where those paths carry volume
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Data policy, its apply-to configuration, the import and API volume on that table, and the records created that would have failed the policy.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate exclusion for a controlled bulk load.

rules.title: UI Policy with a script where declarative configuration suffices
rules.whatItMeans: A UI Policy uses a script where declarative configuration would suffice.
rules.whyItMatters: Harder to read, harder to maintain, and invisible to anyone reviewing the declarative configuration. Low consequence, real accumulation.
rules.sourceTables: UI policy script fields, action equivalence analysis
rules.detectionLogic: UI policies with scripts performing only actions expressible declaratively
rules.threshold: Action classification configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — equivalence judgement.
rules.evidenceToShow: Policy, its script, the declarative equivalent, and the table and form.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Scripts performing logic beyond the declarative model.

rules.title: UI Policy with no condition
rules.whatItMeans: A UI Policy has no condition and applies unconditionally.
rules.whyItMatters: Applies on every form load for every record. Usually indicates the policy was meant to be conditional and the condition was never added.
rules.sourceTables: UI policy condition field
rules.detectionLogic: Active UI policies with empty condition
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Policy list with table, form, its actions, and form view volume.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Policies genuinely intended to apply always.

rules.title: Data Policy inactive but relied upon by process documentation
rules.whatItMeans: A Data Policy is inactive while process documentation relies on it.
rules.whyItMatters: The control is documented as present and is switched off. For audit purposes this is worse than never having had it, because the documentation asserts a control that does not exist.
rules.sourceTables: Data policy active flag, references from knowledge and process documentation where available
rules.detectionLogic: Inactive data policies on fields that process documentation or a control register references
rules.threshold: Requires documentation or control register linkage
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — depends on documentation being introspectable or supplied.
rules.evidenceToShow: Policy, its deactivation date and user, the documentation referencing it, and the records created since that would have failed it.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Policy superseded by an equivalent control.
rules.crossDomainLink: Documented control that does not exist

rules.title: Field mandatory in UI Policy but nullable in dictionary
rules.whatItMeans: A field is mandatory in a UI Policy but nullable in the dictionary.
rules.whyItMatters: The narrower form of PLT-084, at the dictionary level. The database will accept null regardless of what the UI enforces.
rules.sourceTables: UI policy mandatory actions, sys_dictionary mandatory attribute
rules.detectionLogic: Fields mandatory in an active UI policy with dictionary mandatory false and no data policy
rules.threshold: Field-level comparison across all three layers
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the configuration comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Field, UI policy state, dictionary state, data policy state, and the null record count.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Conditional mandatory that the dictionary cannot express.
rules.crossDomainLink: Enforcement gap at the dictionary layer

rules.title: Three generations of automation (business rule, workflow, flow) performing the same function
rules.whatItMeans: Three generations of automation — business rule, legacy workflow, and Flow Designer — perform the same function on the same table.
rules.whyItMatters: The estate has accumulated logic without retiring any. Nobody knows which one actually governs the outcome, and changing behaviour requires finding all three. This is the single most common source of unexplained platform behaviour.
rules.sourceTables: sys_script, wf_workflow, sys_hub_flow trigger conditions and target fields on the same table
rules.detectionLogic: Tables where business rules, workflows and flows all trigger on overlapping conditions and write overlapping fields
rules.threshold: Overlap analysis across all three mechanisms
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — functional overlap detection is inferential. Report all three implementations for human comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table, the three implementations with their triggers and targets, execution volumes, and the overlapping fields.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate layering with clearly separated scope.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — consolidation is an architecture programme, not a fix
rules.crossDomainLink: Root cause of unexplained platform behaviour

rules.title: Legacy Workflow still active where Flow Designer equivalents exist
rules.whatItMeans: Legacy Workflow remains active where Flow Designer equivalents exist.
rules.whyItMatters: Legacy Workflow is maintenance-mode technology. Running critical automation on it is accumulating debt against a deadline nobody has set but that will arrive.
rules.sourceTables: wf_workflow active versions and execution volume, sys_hub_flow coverage of the same functions
rules.detectionLogic: Active workflows with execution volume where equivalent flow capability exists
rules.threshold: Equivalence assessment by function and trigger
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — equivalence is a migration judgement.
rules.evidenceToShow: Workflow, execution volume, the table and trigger, the equivalent flow capability, and the migration complexity indicators.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Workflows using capabilities Flow Designer does not yet cover.

rules.title: Flows and workflows both triggering on the same table and condition
rules.whatItMeans: Flows and workflows both trigger on the same table and condition.
rules.whyItMatters: Both execute. Either the work happens twice or the two produce conflicting outcomes, and which one wins depends on timing.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow and wf_workflow trigger conditions by table
rules.detectionLogic: Table and condition combinations with both an active flow and an active workflow triggering
rules.threshold: Condition overlap analysis
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — condition overlap detection.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table, the flow and workflow, their conditions, execution volumes, and the fields each writes.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate parallel operation during a migration cutover.

rules.title: Flow with no error handling path
rules.whatItMeans: A flow has no error handling path.
rules.whyItMatters: When a step fails the flow stops silently. The record is left mid-process, the user is not told, and there is no queue of failures anyone monitors.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow logic, error handling step presence
rules.detectionLogic: Active flows with no error handling or failure path configured
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; escalate for flows on user-facing or integration paths
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on flow logic introspection.
rules.evidenceToShow: Flow, its steps, absent error handling, execution volume, failure count, and the records currently stuck mid-flow.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Trivial flows where failure is inconsequential.

rules.title: Flow referencing a deleted or inactive object
rules.whatItMeans: A flow references an object that has been deleted or made inactive.
rules.whyItMatters: The flow fails at that step, every time it reaches it. Silent until somebody notices the outcome is missing.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow step references, target object existence and state
rules.detectionLogic: Flow step references to records, tables, fields or actions that no longer exist or are inactive
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on reference existence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Flow, the step, the missing reference, execution volume, failure count since the reference broke, and the records affected.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Reference in a conditional branch never reached.

rules.title: Flow stuck in an executing state beyond threshold
rules.whatItMeans: Flow contexts are stuck in an executing state beyond any reasonable duration.
rules.whyItMatters: The flow never completes. The record sits mid-process indefinitely and the context table accumulates.
rules.sourceTables: sys_flow_context state and duration
rules.detectionLogic: Flow contexts in an executing state beyond duration threshold
rules.threshold: Threshold configurable; default 24 hours for non-wait flows
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on state and duration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Contexts by flow with duration, the step they are stuck at, the records involved, and their business state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Flows with legitimate long waits, such as approvals. Exclude wait steps.
rules.crossDomainLink: Records stuck mid-process; context table growth

rules.title: Flow execution failure rate above threshold
rules.whatItMeans: Flow execution failure rate exceeds threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: The automation is unreliable. Users and downstream processes receive inconsistent outcomes with no pattern they can predict.
rules.sourceTables: sys_flow_context outcome distribution by flow
rules.detectionLogic: Flows with failure rate above threshold, ranked by failure volume
rules.threshold: Threshold default 5%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on outcome distribution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Flow, execution and failure counts, failure rate, the failing steps, and the records affected.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Flows where failure is an expected outcome for some inputs.

rules.title: Flow triggered on every insert with no condition
rules.whatItMeans: A flow triggers on every insert with no condition.
rules.whyItMatters: Executes for every record regardless of relevance. Flow execution is heavier than a business rule, so the cost per unnecessary execution is higher.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow trigger configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Flows with record-created triggers and empty conditions on tables above a volume threshold
rules.threshold: Volume threshold configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on trigger configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Flow, its trigger, the table and insert volume, execution count, and the proportion of executions that take the meaningful branch.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Flows that genuinely apply to all records.

rules.title: Subflow recursion
rules.whatItMeans: Subflow calls form a recursive cycle.
rules.whyItMatters: Each invocation calls back into the chain. Execution multiplies and can exhaust the flow engine, affecting unrelated automation.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow subflow call graph, cycle detection
rules.detectionLogic: Subflow call graphs containing cycles
rules.threshold: Any cycle
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — call graph from static flow logic.
rules.evidenceToShow: The cycle with each flow, the entry point, execution volume, and the context accumulation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Bounded recursion with a documented guard.

rules.title: Flow with hardcoded credentials or endpoints
rules.whatItMeans: A flow contains hardcoded credentials or endpoints.
rules.whyItMatters: Same exposure as PLT-047 and PLT-072, in flow logic. Flow definitions are frequently exported and shared, which widens the exposure further.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow step inputs and script steps, credential and endpoint pattern detection
rules.detectionLogic: Flow steps containing credential, token or embedded-credential URL patterns
rules.threshold: Pattern set configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% on pattern detection. Report location and type only.
rules.evidenceToShow: COUNT AND LOCATION ONLY — flow, step, pattern type. Never reproduce the value.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Placeholder values in an inactive flow.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — rotation and vault migration with security involvement
rules.crossDomainLink: Security exposure; route to security immediately

rules.title: Flow with no owner or inactive owner
rules.whatItMeans: A flow has no owner, or the owner is inactive.
rules.whyItMatters: When it fails, nobody knows who owns the logic. Flows are typically more complex than rules, so the knowledge loss is greater.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow owner and created_by, sys_user.active
rules.detectionLogic: Active flows with empty owner or an owner resolving to an inactive user
rules.threshold: Report the two cases separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on user state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Flow list with owner state, execution volume, failure rate, and creation date.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Ownership held at application level.

rules.title: Orphaned flows with no trigger and no caller
rules.whatItMeans: Orphaned flows exist with no trigger and no caller.
rules.whyItMatters: Cannot execute. Adds upgrade review surface and clutters the flow designer for the people maintaining the real ones.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow trigger configuration, subflow caller references
rules.detectionLogic: Flows with no trigger and no references as a subflow
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — dynamic subflow invocation may not be detected.
rules.evidenceToShow: Flow list with creation date, size, and the reference scan scope applied.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Flows invoked dynamically or through an API.

rules.title: Workflow versions accumulating without cleanup
rules.whatItMeans: Workflow versions accumulate with no cleanup.
rules.whyItMatters: Each published change creates a version and they are never removed. Table growth, slower workflow loading, and a version list nobody can navigate.
rules.sourceTables: wf_workflow_version counts per workflow
rules.detectionLogic: Workflows with version counts above threshold
rules.threshold: Threshold default 20 versions
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on version counts.
rules.evidenceToShow: Workflow, version count, the active version, creation dates, and the table size contribution.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Versions retained deliberately for audit.

rules.title: Flow performing synchronous integration calls in a user-facing path
rules.whatItMeans: A flow performs synchronous integration calls in a user-facing path.
rules.whyItMatters: The user waits for an external system inside their own transaction. Same defect as PLT-049 in the flow engine, and flows make it easier to introduce accidentally.
rules.sourceTables: sys_hub_flow step types and execution mode, trigger type
rules.detectionLogic: Flows with synchronous outbound integration steps triggered from user-facing operations
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — step type and mode from flow introspection.
rules.evidenceToShow: Flow, the integration step and endpoint, its execution mode, the trigger, and the transaction time distribution.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Calls with tight timeouts on a rarely used path.
rules.crossDomainLink: Couples user transactions to external availability

rules.title: Long-running flow contexts accumulating in the context table
rules.whatItMeans: Long-running flow contexts accumulate in the context table.
rules.whyItMatters: Table growth and engine load. Related to PLT-096 but measured as accumulation rather than per-record, so it catches the slow build-up that individual stuck contexts do not reveal.
rules.sourceTables: sys_flow_context row count, age distribution, growth trend
rules.detectionLogic: Context table growth rate and the age distribution of non-terminal contexts
rules.threshold: Age and growth thresholds configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on counts and ages.
rules.evidenceToShow: Context count by flow and state, age distribution, growth trend, and table size.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Long-running approval flows that legitimately hold contexts.

rules.title: Scheduled jobs overlapping their own next execution (never completing)
rules.whatItMeans: Scheduled jobs overlap their own next execution — the job is still running when it is scheduled to start again.
rules.whyItMatters: The job never completes a full cycle. Executions stack, the queue grows, and each run competes with the previous one for the same resources.
rules.sourceTables: sysauto schedule intervals, execution start and end timestamps
rules.detectionLogic: Jobs whose average or maximum duration exceeds their scheduled interval
rules.threshold: Compare against both average and maximum duration
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the duration-versus-interval comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job, interval, duration distribution, overlap frequency, and the concurrent execution count.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Jobs with built-in concurrency guards.

rules.title: Jobs clustered in the same window causing contention
rules.whatItMeans: Scheduled jobs cluster in the same execution window, causing contention.
rules.whyItMatters: Twenty jobs at midnight compete for the same worker threads and database capacity. Each takes longer than it would alone, and the aggregate can push past the maintenance window.
rules.sourceTables: sysauto schedule times, execution duration and concurrency analysis
rules.detectionLogic: Time windows with job concurrency above threshold, with the aggregate duration
rules.threshold: Concurrency threshold configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on schedule analysis.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job distribution by scheduled time, the clustered windows, aggregate duration, and the transaction performance during those windows.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate clustering with adequate capacity.

rules.title: Job with a query that scans an unbounded table
rules.whatItMeans: A scheduled job runs a query that scans an unbounded table.
rules.whyItMatters: Same defect as PLT-039, with the additional property that it runs unattended on a schedule. Failures and slowdowns are invisible until the window is missed.
rules.sourceTables: sysauto_script script bodies, query construction, target table row counts
rules.detectionLogic: Job scripts with queries on large tables and no setLimit or restrictive encoded query
rules.threshold: Row threshold configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — static query analysis.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job, the query, the target table row count, execution duration trend, and the memory profile.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Queries with inherently restrictive encoded queries.

rules.title: Job execution duration trending upward toward its interval
rules.whatItMeans: Job execution duration is trending upward toward its scheduled interval.
rules.whyItMatters: Predictable future failure. The job works until the day duration crosses interval, then PLT-106 begins and the cause is not obvious.
rules.sourceTables: Job execution duration across runs, trend analysis, scheduled interval
rules.detectionLogic: Jobs with positive duration trend projected to exceed interval within the horizon
rules.threshold: Horizon default 90 days; requires at least 5 runs
rules.confidenceBasis: Trend confidence from run count and variance. State the projection.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job, duration trend, interval, projected crossover date, and the data volume driving the growth.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Duration growth from a one-time data load.

rules.title: Job failing repeatedly with no alerting
rules.whatItMeans: A job fails repeatedly with no alerting configured.
rules.whyItMatters: The job stops doing its work and nobody is told. Whatever it maintained — archival, reconciliation, notification — silently stops.
rules.sourceTables: Job execution outcomes, failure counts, alerting configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Jobs with failure rate above threshold and no failure alerting or notification
rules.threshold: Failure threshold default 20%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on outcomes and alerting configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job, failure count and rate, error class, absent alerting, and what the job maintains.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Failures monitored through an external mechanism.

rules.title: Job active but with no execution record
rules.whatItMeans: A job is active with no execution record at all.
rules.whyItMatters: Scheduled and never running. Either the trigger is broken or the job was never properly activated, and whatever it was meant to do has never happened.
rules.sourceTables: sysauto active flag, sys_trigger records, execution history
rules.detectionLogic: Active jobs with no execution records and age above threshold
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 30 days or 3 intervals, whichever is longer
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on execution record absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job, its schedule, creation date, the trigger record state, and what it was intended to do.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Jobs with a future start date.

rules.title: Job performing record deletion with no archival
rules.whatItMeans: A job performs record deletion with no archival.
rules.whyItMatters: Data is destroyed on a schedule with no recovery path. Where the data is subject to retention obligations this is a compliance exposure as well as an operational one.
rules.sourceTables: sysauto_script script bodies, delete operation detection, archival configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Jobs performing deleteMultiple or deleteRecord with no corresponding archival step
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — delete operation detection from script analysis.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job, the delete operation, the target table and query, the volume deleted per run, and the retention policy for that table.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deletion of genuinely transient data with a documented policy.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — deletion review requires data ownership input
rules.crossDomainLink: Irrecoverable data loss; DPDP retention relevance

rules.title: Job with no owner or inactive owner
rules.whatItMeans: A job has no owner, or the owner is an inactive user.
rules.whyItMatters: When it fails, nobody knows what it does or whether it matters. Jobs are less visible than rules, so the knowledge loss is more complete.
rules.sourceTables: sysauto owner and created_by, sys_user.active
rules.detectionLogic: Active jobs with empty owner or an owner resolving to an inactive user
rules.threshold: Report the two cases separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on user state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job list with owner state, schedule, last execution, and what it operates on.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Ownership at the application level.

rules.title: Job running more frequently than its output is consumed
rules.whatItMeans: A job runs more frequently than its output is consumed.
rules.whyItMatters: Hourly generation of a report read weekly. Pure waste, and it competes for capacity with jobs that matter.
rules.sourceTables: Job schedule interval, output consumption indicators such as report views or downstream record creation
rules.detectionLogic: Jobs whose execution frequency materially exceeds their output consumption rate
rules.threshold: Consumption measurement depends on the job type; state the method
rules.confidenceBasis: 80% — consumption inference varies by job type and is the weakest part of this rule.
rules.evidenceToShow: Job, interval, output type, consumption rate, and the execution cost per run.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Output consumed through a channel not measurable.

rules.title: Event queue depth beyond threshold
rules.whatItMeans: The event queue depth exceeds threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: Events are queued rather than processed. Notifications, script actions and downstream automation all lag by the queue depth, and during an incident that lag is when it matters most.
rules.sourceTables: sysevent queue depth and age aggregates
rules.detectionLogic: Event queue depth and oldest-event age against thresholds
rules.threshold: Age is the more meaningful threshold; default 10 minutes
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on queue aggregates.
rules.evidenceToShow: Queue depth and age trend, event type distribution, processing rate versus creation rate, and the consumers affected.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Transient backlog during a known bulk operation.

rules.title: Events registered with no script action or notification consuming them
rules.whatItMeans: Events are registered and fired with no script action or notification consuming them.
rules.whyItMatters: The event is generated, queued and processed to no effect. Pure queue load with no function.
rules.sourceTables: sysevent_register records, sysevent_script_action and notification consumers, event fire volume
rules.detectionLogic: Registered events with fire volume and no active consumer
rules.threshold: Any occurrence with non-zero volume
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on consumer registration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Event, fire volume, absent consumers, and the queue load it contributes.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Events consumed by an external subscriber.

rules.title: Event flooding from a single source
rules.whatItMeans: Event flooding from a single source.
rules.whyItMatters: One source dominates the queue and delays everything else. Usually a misconfigured rule or integration firing events in a loop.
rules.sourceTables: sysevent volume by name and source
rules.detectionLogic: Event sources whose volume exceeds threshold share of total
rules.threshold: Share threshold default 30%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on volume distribution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Event volume by name and source, the flooding source, its trigger, and the queue depth during flood periods.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimately high-volume events.

rules.title: sys\_trigger backlog growing
rules.whatItMeans: The sys_trigger backlog is growing.
rules.whyItMatters: Scheduled and async work is not being dispatched. Jobs run late or not at all, and the symptom appears as unrelated functional failures across the instance.
rules.sourceTables: sys_trigger row counts, next action timestamps, backlog trend
rules.detectionLogic: sys_trigger records with next action in the past, counted and trended
rules.threshold: Threshold configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on counts and timestamps.
rules.evidenceToShow: Backlog count and trend, the oldest overdue trigger, the job types affected, and the worker capacity.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Transient backlog after a node restart.

rules.title: Async job queue processing lag
rules.whatItMeans: Async job queue processing lag exceeds threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: Async work is queued rather than executed. Anything deferred to async — integrations, notifications, bulk updates — runs late, and the deferral was supposed to make things faster.
rules.sourceTables: Async queue depth and processing lag
rules.detectionLogic: Async queue lag above threshold, trended
rules.threshold: Lag threshold configurable, default 15 minutes
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on queue metrics.
rules.evidenceToShow: Lag trend, queue depth, the job types queued, and the worker capacity and utilisation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Transient lag during a bulk operation.

rules.title: Admin role count above threshold or trending up
rules.whatItMeans: The admin role count exceeds threshold, or is trending upward.
rules.whyItMatters: Admin bypasses every ACL in the instance. The count is the single clearest measure of how much of the access control model is actually in force, and a rising trend means it is eroding.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user_has_role for admin and equivalent roles, sys_user.active, trend across snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(active users holding admin, directly or through role nesting), with trend
rules.threshold: Threshold relative to estate size; default 10 or 1% of fulfillers, whichever is lower
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the count after nesting resolution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Admin holder list with grant date, granting user, group path where nested, last login, and the trend.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Break-glass accounts that are documented and monitored.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — role removal is an access decision requiring approval
rules.crossDomainLink: The headline access finding; route to security and audit

rules.title: ACLs with true as the condition or no condition at all
rules.whatItMeans: ACLs exist with a condition of 'true' or no condition at all.
rules.whyItMatters: The ACL evaluates to permitted for everyone who reaches it. It appears in the ACL list as a control and grants unconditional access.
rules.sourceTables: sys_security_acl condition and script fields
rules.detectionLogic: Active ACLs with empty condition and empty script, or with a script returning true unconditionally
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; escalate on sensitive tables
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on empty conditions. 95% on unconditional script detection.
rules.evidenceToShow: ACL, table and field, operation, its condition and script, the roles required, and the record volume it governs.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: ACLs deliberately permissive where the role requirement is the control.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 — condition addition as update set, tested carefully
rules.crossDomainLink: Ineffective access control presented as a control

rules.title: Tables with no ACL coverage at all
rules.whatItMeans: Tables exist with no ACL coverage at all.
rules.whyItMatters: Access falls back to a parent table ACL or to the default, neither of which was designed for this table. Custom tables holding sensitive data are the common case.
rules.sourceTables: sys_db_object table list, sys_security_acl coverage with hierarchy resolution
rules.detectionLogic: Tables with record volume and no ACL at table or field level, after parent inheritance resolution
rules.threshold: Inheritance resolution mandatory or this rule produces mass false positives
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% after correct inheritance resolution. Resolution errors are the main failure mode — test it.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table, row count, ACL coverage state, the inherited ACLs applying, and the roles that can currently read and write.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Coverage through parent inheritance that the resolution missed. Verify the resolution logic before raising at volume.
rules.crossDomainLink: Unintended access model on custom tables

rules.title: Elevated privilege granted with no approval or change trail
rules.whatItMeans: Elevated privilege has been granted with no approval or change trail.
rules.whyItMatters: Someone has admin or a high-privilege role and there is no record of who authorised it. In a regulated entity this is an audit exception independent of whether the grant was appropriate.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user_has_role grant records and audit, change and approval record correlation
rules.detectionLogic: Elevated role grants with no corresponding approval or change record in the window
rules.threshold: Elevated role set configurable; correlation window configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — depends on approval records being linkable to grants.
rules.evidenceToShow: The grant with date, granting user, recipient, the role, and the absence of approval or change lineage.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Grants made through an approved bulk provisioning process.

rules.title: Role nesting producing unintended effective permissions
rules.whatItMeans: Role nesting produces effective permissions that were not intended.
rules.whyItMatters: A role three levels down contains admin. Nobody granting the outer role knew. Effective permissions diverge from stated permissions, and the divergence is invisible without traversing the graph.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user_role_contains nesting graph, effective role resolution
rules.detectionLogic: Roles whose transitive closure includes elevated roles not evident from the role name or description
rules.threshold: Elevated role set configurable; full transitive closure required
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the graph traversal. The judgement that it was unintended is inferred.
rules.evidenceToShow: Role, its nesting path to the elevated role, the users holding it, and the effective permissions each gains.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate and documented nesting.
rules.crossDomainLink: Effective permissions diverge from stated permissions

rules.title: ACL script returning true unconditionally
rules.whatItMeans: An ACL script returns true unconditionally.
rules.whyItMatters: The narrower, harder-to-spot form of PLT-121. The ACL has a script, so it appears to implement logic, and the logic grants everything.
rules.sourceTables: sys_security_acl script bodies, return path analysis
rules.detectionLogic: ACL scripts whose every return path evaluates to true
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — return path analysis; complex scripts may be misjudged.
rules.evidenceToShow: ACL, the script, its return paths, the table and operation, and the record volume governed.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Scripts with conditional logic the analysis did not follow.

rules.title: Write ACL absent where read ACL exists on sensitive tables
rules.whatItMeans: A read ACL exists on a sensitive table with no corresponding write ACL.
rules.whyItMatters: Read is controlled and write is not. Anyone who reaches the table can modify it, which is the more damaging of the two operations.
rules.sourceTables: sys_security_acl operation coverage by table, sensitive table classification
rules.detectionLogic: Sensitive tables with read ACL coverage and no write, create or delete ACL
rules.threshold: Sensitive table set from classification or from DQ-139 detection
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on ACL coverage after inheritance resolution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table, its sensitivity classification, the read ACLs present, the absent write ACLs, and the roles that can currently write.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Write controlled through a data policy or business rule.

rules.title: ACLs on sensitive fields (financial, personal, credential) missing
rules.whatItMeans: Field-level ACLs are missing on sensitive fields — financial, personal or credential.
rules.whyItMatters: Table-level access grants the whole record including fields that should be restricted. Field-level protection is the mechanism for that and it is absent.
rules.sourceTables: Sensitive field classification, sys_security_acl field-level coverage
rules.detectionLogic: Fields classified sensitive with no field-level ACL
rules.threshold: Sensitive field set from classification or content detection
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on ACL coverage. Field classification confidence depends on its source.
rules.evidenceToShow: Field, table, classification, absent field ACL, the table-level ACL in force, and the roles that can read it.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Protection at table level genuinely adequate for that field.

rules.title: snc\_internal or public-facing access on tables holding personal data
rules.whatItMeans: Tables holding personal data are accessible via snc_internal or public-facing configuration.
rules.whyItMatters: Personal data reachable by the broadest access class on the instance, or by unauthenticated paths. The most serious access finding in the catalogue for a DPDP-regulated entity.
rules.sourceTables: Personal data table classification, ACL role requirements, public page and unauthenticated endpoint configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Personal-data tables whose ACLs require only snc_internal, or which are reachable from public pages or unauthenticated endpoints
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on ACL role requirements. Public reachability at 90%.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table, its personal data classification, record volume, the ACL role requirement, and the public or internal access path.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Tables misclassified as holding personal data.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 2 — escalate immediately, do not batch with routine findings
rules.crossDomainLink: Most serious DPDP access exposure; route to security immediately

rules.title: Inactive users still holding roles
rules.whatItMeans: Inactive users still hold roles.
rules.whyItMatters: Access persists after departure. The account cannot log in interactively but the role grant remains, which matters for API access, delegation, and if the account is ever reactivated.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user.active, sys_user_has_role
rules.detectionLogic: Role grants held by users with active=false
rules.threshold: Report elevated roles separately from ordinary ones
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on user state and role grants.
rules.evidenceToShow: User list with deactivation date, the roles held, whether any are elevated, and any API or integration use of the account since.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Accounts deactivated within a grace period pending formal offboarding.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — role removal is an access decision
rules.crossDomainLink: Joins DQ-117; access persistence after departure

rules.title: Service accounts with interactive login enabled
rules.whatItMeans: Service accounts have interactive login enabled.
rules.whyItMatters: A service account credential is typically long-lived, widely known within a team, and not subject to MFA. Interactive login on it removes the distinction between a service identity and a person.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user web_service_access_only flag, account type indicators, login history
rules.detectionLogic: Accounts classified as service accounts with interactive login permitted
rules.threshold: Service account classification from naming, roles and usage pattern
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — service account classification is inferred.
rules.evidenceToShow: Account, its classification basis, interactive login configuration, login history, and the roles held.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Accounts genuinely requiring interactive use.
rules.crossDomainLink: Identity model erosion; route to security

rules.title: Roles granted directly to users rather than via groups
rules.whatItMeans: Roles are granted directly to users rather than through groups.
rules.whyItMatters: Direct grants are invisible to group-based recertification and do not follow the person when they move. Access accumulates and is never reviewed.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user_has_role grant source, group-derived versus direct
rules.detectionLogic: Direct role grants as a share of total grants, by role and by user
rules.threshold: Report ratio and the elevated-role subset separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on grant source.
rules.evidenceToShow: Direct grant ratio, the roles most commonly granted directly, the users holding them, and whether a group exists that would grant the same.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Roles for which no appropriate group exists.

rules.title: Roles with no users assigned
rules.whatItMeans: Roles exist with no users assigned.
rules.whyItMatters: Either the role is obsolete, or it is a container in a nesting structure. Housekeeping, but a large population of empty roles makes access review harder.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user_role records, sys_user_has_role counts, sys_user_role_contains
rules.detectionLogic: Roles with zero direct and zero derived holders
rules.threshold: Exclude roles that are containers in an active nesting structure
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on holder counts after nesting resolution.
rules.evidenceToShow: Role list with creation date, nesting position, the ACLs referencing them, and holder count.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Roles reserved for a future application.

rules.title: Groups with no members holding elevated roles
rules.whatItMeans: Groups holding elevated roles have no members.
rules.whyItMatters: The group is a live privilege container waiting for a member. Adding anyone to it grants elevated access without any role grant appearing in the audit trail.
rules.sourceTables: sys_user_group records, group role grants, active membership
rules.detectionLogic: Groups granting elevated roles with zero active members
rules.threshold: Elevated role set configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on membership and role grants.
rules.evidenceToShow: Group, the elevated roles it grants, membership history, last membership change, and who can add members.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Break-glass groups documented and monitored.
rules.crossDomainLink: Latent privilege escalation path; route to security

rules.title: No access recertification or review process evidenced
rules.whatItMeans: No access recertification or review process is evidenced.
rules.whyItMatters: Access is granted and never reviewed. Every other access finding in this group accumulates because nothing removes it, which makes this the Systemic root of the access dimension.
rules.sourceTables: Recertification or attestation records for role and group membership, review task history
rules.detectionLogic: Absence of recertification records covering role and group grants within a review period
rules.threshold: Review period from policy; default annual
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on record absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Recertification record state, the population that should be reviewed, grant ages, and the elevated role holders never reviewed.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Recertification conducted in an external IGA platform with evidence.
rules.crossDomainLink: Root cause of access accumulation; regulatory evidence gap

rules.title: ACL overriding an OOB ACL with weaker conditions
rules.whatItMeans: A custom ACL overrides an out-of-box ACL with weaker conditions.
rules.whyItMatters: Platform protection replaced with something less restrictive. The OOB ACL was there for a reason and the reason is usually not documented in the replacement.
rules.sourceTables: sys_security_acl records, OOB ACL inventory, condition comparison by table, field and operation
rules.detectionLogic: Custom ACLs on the same table, field and operation as an OOB ACL, with weaker role or condition requirements
rules.threshold: Weakness comparison across role requirement and condition restrictiveness
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — relative restrictiveness comparison is partly a judgement.
rules.evidenceToShow: Custom ACL, the OOB ACL it shadows, both conditions and role requirements, and the access difference.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate and documented relaxation.

rules.title: Impersonation used in production with no audit review
rules.whatItMeans: Impersonation is used in production with no audit review.
rules.whyItMatters: One user acting as another. Legitimate for support, and it obscures attribution in the audit trail unless the impersonation records are themselves reviewed.
rules.sourceTables: Impersonation audit records, volume by impersonator and target, review evidence
rules.detectionLogic: Impersonation events in production with no corresponding review record
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report volume by impersonator
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on impersonation records.
rules.evidenceToShow: Impersonation volume by user, the targets, the actions taken while impersonating, and the absence of review.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Impersonation reviewed through an external process.
rules.crossDomainLink: Attribution gap in the audit trail

rules.title: Integration user holding admin role
rules.whatItMeans: An integration user holds the admin role.
rules.whyItMatters: The credential is stored in an external system, often in configuration, and it grants unrestricted access. Compromise of any system holding it is compromise of the entire instance.
rules.sourceTables: Integration user identification, sys_user_has_role, web service access configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Users classified as integration accounts holding admin or equivalent
rules.threshold: Integration account classification from web_service_access_only, naming and usage
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — integration account classification is inferred but usually clear.
rules.evidenceToShow: Account, its classification basis, the admin grant with date and granting user, the systems using it, and the minimum role set its actual operations require.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely requires broad access. Recommend a scoped role set regardless.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — role reduction requires testing against the integration
rules.crossDomainLink: Highest-severity integration security finding; route to security

rules.title: Basic authentication in use on any inbound or outbound integration
rules.whatItMeans: Basic authentication is in use on inbound or outbound integrations.
rules.whyItMatters: Credentials transmitted on every call, typically long-lived and rarely rotated. For a regulated entity this is a control finding regardless of transport encryption.
rules.sourceTables: REST and SOAP message authentication configuration, inbound web service authentication
rules.detectionLogic: Integrations configured with basic authentication
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; report inbound and outbound separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on authentication configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, direction, endpoint, authentication type, call volume, and the OAuth capability available.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Endpoints that support no other mechanism. Document and compensate.
rules.crossDomainLink: Security control finding; route to security

rules.title: Credentials stored outside the credential vault
rules.whatItMeans: Integration credentials are stored outside the credential vault.
rules.whyItMatters: Secrets in configuration tables rather than in a managed store. Captured in update sets, readable by anyone with the relevant table access, and not subject to rotation controls.
rules.sourceTables: Credential storage configuration, vault integration state, connection and credential alias usage
rules.detectionLogic: Integrations with credentials stored inline rather than through a credential or connection alias
rules.threshold: Fires where vault or alias capability exists
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, credential storage mechanism, the vault capability available, and the roles that can read the stored value.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: No vault capability available. Report as a capability gap.

rules.title: Inbound integration bypassing IRE or Data Policy
rules.whatItMeans: Inbound integrations bypass the identification engine or data policies.
rules.whyItMatters: Data enters the platform without passing the controls designed to validate and reconcile it. The direct cause of a large share of CMDB duplicates and invalid values.
rules.sourceTables: Inbound integration write paths, IRE usage, data policy apply-to configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Inbound integrations writing directly to tables without IRE processing or data policy application
rules.threshold: Scope to tables where IRE or data policies exist
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — write path analysis.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, its write path, the tables, IRE and data policy bypass, the record volume created, and the duplicate and validity defects attributable.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Bulk migration with deliberate bypass under a documented plan.
rules.crossDomainLink: Root cause of CMDB-046 and CMDB-029

rules.title: Integration with no error handling or retry
rules.whatItMeans: An integration has no error handling or retry configuration.
rules.whyItMatters: A single transient failure produces a permanent data gap. With retry, the same failure self-heals and nobody needs to know.
rules.sourceTables: Integration error handling and retry configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Integrations with no retry or error handling configured
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, retry and error configuration, historical transient failure count, and the data gaps each produced.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Semantics where retry is inappropriate, such as non-idempotent operations.

rules.title: Integration failure rate above threshold
rules.whatItMeans: Integration failure rate exceeds threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: The integration is unreliable. Downstream data is incomplete in ways that are intermittent and therefore hard to characterise.
rules.sourceTables: Integration execution outcomes, failure counts by integration
rules.detectionLogic: Integrations with failure rate above threshold, ranked by failure volume
rules.threshold: Threshold default 5%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on outcome records.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, execution and failure counts, failure rate and trend, error classes, and the affected downstream data.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Failures expected for some inputs.

rules.title: Integration with no rate limiting configured
rules.whatItMeans: An integration has no rate limiting configured.
rules.whyItMatters: An upstream system can flood the instance. A misbehaving integration partner becomes a platform availability event, and there is no mechanism to contain it.
rules.sourceTables: sys_rate_limit_rule coverage, inbound integration volume
rules.detectionLogic: Inbound integrations with no covering rate limit rule
rules.threshold: Any occurrence; escalate for high-volume or external-facing integrations
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on rule coverage.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, call volume and peak rate, absent rate limit coverage, and the transaction impact during peak periods.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Rate limiting applied at an upstream gateway.

rules.title: Endpoints using HTTP rather than HTTPS
rules.whatItMeans: Integration endpoints use HTTP rather than HTTPS.
rules.whyItMatters: Data and credentials in plaintext across the network. Straightforward finding, and it still appears regularly on internal endpoints where people assume the network is trusted.
rules.sourceTables: REST and SOAP message endpoint URLs, protocol
rules.detectionLogic: Integration endpoints with an http:// scheme
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the URL scheme.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, endpoint, direction, authentication type, call volume, and the data transmitted.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Internal endpoints on a segmented network with documented acceptance.

rules.title: OAuth tokens with no expiry or excessive lifetime
rules.whatItMeans: OAuth tokens have no expiry, or an excessive lifetime.
rules.whyItMatters: A long-lived token is functionally a permanent credential with none of the controls a password carries. Revocation becomes the only mitigation and it is rarely exercised.
rules.sourceTables: oauth_entity and oauth_credential expiry configuration
rules.detectionLogic: OAuth configurations with no token expiry or lifetime above threshold
rules.threshold: Lifetime threshold configurable; default 90 days for refresh tokens
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: OAuth entity, token lifetime, the roles the token grants, the systems holding it, and the last rotation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Lifetime required by an external system's constraints.

rules.title: Integration writing directly to tables, bypassing business logic
rules.whatItMeans: An integration writes directly to tables, bypassing business logic.
rules.whyItMatters: Business rules, flows and data policies do not fire. Downstream effects that should follow the write do not happen, and the record is created in a state the process model does not expect.
rules.sourceTables: Integration write paths, setWorkflow usage, direct table API usage
rules.detectionLogic: Integrations writing with workflow suppressed or through paths that bypass business logic
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — write path and suppression analysis.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration, its write path, the suppressed logic, the tables, the record volume, and the downstream effects that do not occur.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate bypass for performance on a controlled bulk path.

rules.title: Orphaned integrations with no execution in the window
rules.whatItMeans: Orphaned integrations exist with no execution in the observation window.
rules.whyItMatters: Configured, credentialed and unused. Each one is an open door with no traffic, which is an access surface with no offsetting value.
rules.sourceTables: Integration execution history, configuration records
rules.detectionLogic: Integrations with no execution in the window
rules.threshold: Window default 180 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on execution history.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration list with last execution, credentials held, endpoint, and the roles the integration user holds.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Seasonal or disaster-recovery integrations.

rules.title: Duplicate integrations to the same endpoint
rules.whatItMeans: Duplicate integrations point at the same endpoint.
rules.whyItMatters: Two configurations doing the same thing. Changes applied to one leave the other stale, and which one runs depends on what calls it.
rules.sourceTables: Integration endpoint URLs, method and payload comparison
rules.detectionLogic: Integration pairs with matching endpoint and method
rules.threshold: Normalised URL comparison
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — endpoint match is exact; the conclusion of unintended duplication is inferred.
rules.evidenceToShow: Both integrations, their endpoints, methods, callers, execution volumes, and configuration differences.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate separation by environment or purpose.

rules.title: Import sets accumulating without cleanup
rules.whatItMeans: Import set tables accumulate without cleanup.
rules.whyItMatters: Staging data retained indefinitely. Substantial table growth, and where the source data contains personal information it is a retention exposure as well.
rules.sourceTables: Import set table row counts and growth, cleanup job configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Import set tables above size threshold with no cleanup job
rules.threshold: Size threshold configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on counts and configuration.
rules.evidenceToShow: Import set tables with row counts, growth, oldest record, cleanup configuration, and whether the staged data includes personal identifiers.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Retention required for reconciliation evidence.

rules.title: Transform maps with no coalesce, generating duplicates
rules.whatItMeans: Transform maps have no coalesce field configured, generating duplicate records on every run.
rules.whyItMatters: Every import creates new records instead of updating existing ones. On a recurring import this produces duplicates at a predictable rate, and it is one of the most mechanical causes of CMDB duplication.
rules.sourceTables: sys_transform_map and sys_transform_entry coalesce configuration, target table duplicate counts
rules.detectionLogic: Transform maps with no coalesce entry, joined to duplicate counts on their target tables
rules.threshold: Any occurrence on a recurring import
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration. Duplicate attribution at 95%.
rules.evidenceToShow: Transform map, its entries, absent coalesce, import frequency, and the duplicate record count on the target table.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Insert-only maps where duplication is intended.

rules.title: Transform scripts with unhandled errors
rules.whatItMeans: Transform scripts throw unhandled errors.
rules.whyItMatters: Rows fail to transform and are silently skipped. The import reports completion with a lower row count than the source, and nobody reconciles the two.
rules.sourceTables: Transform script errors in the import log, error counts by map
rules.detectionLogic: Transform maps with script error counts above threshold
rules.threshold: Threshold relative to row volume
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on error counts.
rules.evidenceToShow: Transform map, error count and class, sample errors, rows skipped, and the source-to-target row count reconciliation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Errors from genuinely malformed source rows.

rules.title: Data source credentials expired
rules.whatItMeans: Data source credentials have expired.
rules.whyItMatters: The import stops. Data ages from that date, and because the import job still runs and reports completion, nothing signals the failure.
rules.sourceTables: sys_data_source credential references, credential expiry, import execution outcomes
rules.detectionLogic: Data sources whose credentials are expired or failing authentication
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on credential state and import outcomes.
rules.evidenceToShow: Data source, credential state and expiry, last successful import, and the data now ageing as a result.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Credential rotation in progress.
rules.crossDomainLink: Silent import cessation; same pattern as ITOM-017

rules.title: Integration with no documented owner
rules.whatItMeans: An integration has no documented owner.
rules.whyItMatters: When it breaks, or when its access needs reviewing, nobody knows whose it is. Integrations outlive the people who build them more reliably than any other object type.
rules.sourceTables: Integration owner fields, created_by, sys_user.active
rules.detectionLogic: Integrations with no owner, or an owner resolving to an inactive user
rules.threshold: Report the two cases separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on field and user state.
rules.evidenceToShow: Integration list with owner state, endpoint, execution volume, the roles its user holds, and creation date.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Ownership at application level.

rules.title: Skipped updates from the last upgrade never reviewed
rules.whatItMeans: Skipped updates from the last upgrade have never been reviewed.
rules.whyItMatters: At every upgrade, ServiceNow skips updates to records the customer modified. Each skipped update is a platform improvement or fix the instance did not receive, and the list is usually never opened.
rules.sourceTables: sys_upgrade_history and sys_upgrade_history_log, skipped update records and review state
rules.detectionLogic: Skipped updates from the most recent upgrade with no review disposition recorded
rules.threshold: Any unreviewed skipped update; rank by the object's execution volume and criticality
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the skipped update records.
rules.evidenceToShow: Skipped update list ranked by object criticality, the customisation causing each skip, the platform change that was skipped, and the review state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Reviews conducted outside ServiceNow with evidence.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — each disposition is a judgement
rules.crossDomainLink: The single richest source of upgrade debt evidence

rules.title: Modified OOB records count and trend
rules.whatItMeans: The count of modified out-of-box records, and its trend.
rules.whyItMatters: The headline customisation measure. The trend matters more than the count: an estate adding modifications faster than it retires them is accumulating upgrade cost that compounds at every release.
rules.sourceTables: sys_update_version and sys_metadata OOB modification indicators, trend across snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(OOB records with customer modifications), by object type, with trend
rules.threshold: Report by object type; no single threshold
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on modification records.
rules.evidenceToShow: Modified OOB count by object type, trend, the objects most modified, and the skipped update count each has generated.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Modifications required by a genuine functional gap.

rules.title: Customization concentrated in objects ServiceNow actively develops
rules.whatItMeans: Customisation is concentrated in objects that ServiceNow actively develops.
rules.whyItMatters: Modifying a stable object is low risk. Modifying one ServiceNow changes every release guarantees a collision at every upgrade, forever. Concentration here is what makes upgrades expensive.
rules.sourceTables: Modified OOB records, ServiceNow change frequency per object across releases
rules.detectionLogic: Modified OOB objects ranked by the platform's own change frequency for that object
rules.threshold: Change frequency derived from upgrade history across releases
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — change frequency derivation depends on upgrade history depth available.
rules.evidenceToShow: Modified objects ranked by platform change frequency, the skipped updates each has produced, and the projected collisions at the next upgrade.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Modifications to objects the platform rarely changes.

rules.title: Instance more than two families behind current
rules.whatItMeans: The instance is more than two families behind the current release.
rules.whyItMatters: Support, security patches and feature availability all degrade. Each additional family behind makes the eventual upgrade larger and the collision count higher.
rules.sourceTables: Instance version and family, current ServiceNow release
rules.detectionLogic: Instance family compared against current, in family count
rules.threshold: Threshold default 2 families
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on version comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Instance family, current family, families behind, last upgrade date, and the skipped update backlog.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate deferral with documented support arrangements.
rules.crossDomainLink: Compounding upgrade cost and support exposure

rules.title: Global scope customization where scoped apps should be used
rules.whatItMeans: Global scope customisation exists where scoped applications should have been used.
rules.whyItMatters: Global has no boundary, no dependency declaration and no containment. Customisation there is invisible to application-level governance and collides more readily at upgrade.
rules.sourceTables: Custom object scope distribution, scoped application inventory
rules.detectionLogic: Custom objects in global scope that form a coherent functional group suitable for a scoped application
rules.threshold: Grouping by table and function
rules.confidenceBasis: 80% — the judgement that they belong in a scope is inferential.
rules.evidenceToShow: Global custom object inventory grouped by function, their tables, and the scoped applications that exist.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely cross-cutting platform extensions.
rules.rawRemediationLane: Lane 3 — scope migration is a programme

rules.title: Custom tables extending task or cmdb\_ci without justification
rules.whatItMeans: Custom tables extend task or cmdb_ci without justification.
rules.whyItMatters: Extending task inherits the entire task lifecycle, SLA engine and business rule cascade. Extending cmdb_ci inherits identification, reconciliation and health. Both are appropriate sometimes and expensive when they are not.
rules.sourceTables: sys_db_object super_class, custom table identification, usage analysis
rules.detectionLogic: Custom tables extending task or cmdb_ci whose usage does not exercise the inherited capabilities
rules.threshold: Usage assessment from field population and process linkage
rules.confidenceBasis: 80% — whether the extension is justified is a design judgement.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table, its parent, row count, the inherited capabilities, which are actually used, and the rules and SLAs cascading to it.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Extensions that genuinely use the inherited model.

rules.title: Custom fields on OOB tables, unpopulated
rules.whatItMeans: Custom fields on out-of-box tables are unpopulated.
rules.whyItMatters: Schema weight, form clutter and upgrade review surface for data nobody captures. Each one must be assessed at every upgrade.
rules.sourceTables: Custom fields on OOB tables, population rates
rules.detectionLogic: Custom fields on OOB tables with population rate below threshold
rules.threshold: Threshold default 5%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on population rate.
rules.evidenceToShow: Field list with table, population rate, creation date, creating update set, and the forms carrying it.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Fields for a programme not yet live.

rules.title: Custom fields duplicating OOB field function
rules.whatItMeans: Custom fields duplicate the function of an existing out-of-box field.
rules.whyItMatters: Two fields hold the same thing. Reporting splits, integrations pick one, and the platform features that read the OOB field see nothing.
rules.sourceTables: Custom field definitions, OOB field semantics on the same table, population correlation
rules.detectionLogic: Custom fields whose semantics and population correlate with an existing OOB field on the same table
rules.threshold: Semantic matching from name, type and population correlation
rules.confidenceBasis: 80% — semantic equivalence is inferential. Report both fields for human comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Both fields, their types, population rates and correlation, and the platform features reading the OOB field.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Custom field capturing a genuinely distinct attribute.
rules.crossDomainLink: Split data; platform features read the wrong field

rules.title: Deprecated API usage in scripts
rules.whatItMeans: Scripts use deprecated APIs.
rules.whyItMatters: Deprecated APIs are removed eventually. The script works until the release that removes them, and the failure arrives as part of an upgrade with many other changes.
rules.sourceTables: Script bodies across all script object types, deprecated API inventory for the instance version
rules.detectionLogic: Scripts containing calls to APIs marked deprecated in the current or announced releases
rules.threshold: Deprecated API list per release
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — depends on the deprecation list being current.
rules.evidenceToShow: Script, the deprecated API, the release in which it was deprecated, the removal release where announced, and the script's execution volume.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: APIs deprecated with no announced removal.

rules.title: Deprecated plugin still active
rules.whatItMeans: Deprecated plugins remain active.
rules.whyItMatters: The plugin is no longer developed and may be removed. Functionality built on it is on borrowed time, and the migration path narrows each release.
rules.sourceTables: v_plugin active list, deprecation status per instance version
rules.detectionLogic: Active plugins marked deprecated
rules.threshold: Deprecation status from the instance's own plugin metadata
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% where deprecation status is available.
rules.evidenceToShow: Plugin, deprecation status, the functionality depending on it, usage volume, and the replacement path.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deprecated plugin with no replacement available.

rules.title: Customization hotspots — objects modified repeatedly
rules.whatItMeans: Customisation hotspots — objects modified repeatedly over time.
rules.whyItMatters: Repeated modification indicates either an unstable requirement or a design that does not fit. Hotspots are where upgrade collisions concentrate and where defects are most likely.
rules.sourceTables: sys_update_version modification counts per object, trend
rules.detectionLogic: Objects with modification counts above threshold across the window
rules.threshold: Threshold default 5 modifications in 12 months
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on modification counts.
rules.evidenceToShow: Object ranked by modification count, the modifying users and update sets, the skipped updates produced, and the incident correlation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Objects under active development in a live project.
rules.crossDomainLink: Where upgrade collisions and defects concentrate

rules.title: Update sets unclosed, stuck in preview, or with collisions
rules.whatItMeans: Update sets are unclosed, stuck in preview, or carrying unresolved collisions.
rules.whyItMatters: Changes are held in limbo. Unclosed sets can lose changes on capture, preview-stuck sets block promotion, and unresolved collisions mean somebody will eventually force a promotion and overwrite something.
rules.sourceTables: sys_update_set state, sys_remote_update_set preview state, collision records
rules.detectionLogic: Update sets in open state beyond age threshold, in preview beyond threshold, or with unresolved collisions
rules.threshold: Age thresholds configurable; report the three cases separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on set state and collision records.
rules.evidenceToShow: Update set list by state with age, owner, record count, and the collision details for each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Sets deliberately held open for an active project.
rules.crossDomainLink: Release process blockage and overwrite risk

rules.title: Changes made directly in production with no update set lineage
